articles.title: Former Liverpool, Man City, Chelsea and Arsenal star Sterling handed suspended prison sentence
articles.summary: Raheem Sterling avoided jail but was disqualified from driving for two years
articles.content:
Former Liverpool, Man City, Chelsea and Arsenal star Sterling handed suspended prison sentence

Raheem Sterling avoided jail but was disqualified from driving for two years

Last Update:

Former England international Raheem Sterling has been handed a suspended 12-month prison sentence for dangerous driving.

Sterling pleaded guilty to the offence in September after being arrested following a road traffic accident on the M3 motorway in Hampshire on the morning of May 28, 2026.

He also admitted possessing nitrous oxide for wrongful inhalation and failing to provide a specimen for analysis.

The 31-year-old enjoyed a glittering career for club and country, winning 82 England caps as well as four Premier League titles with Manchester City. He started out at Liverpool before spells with City, Chelsea, Arsenal and, most recently, Feyenoord.

articles.title: Cristiano Ronaldo deserves proper Portugal send-off, says former rival Pep Guardiola
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo walked away from international football earlier this month but Pep Guardiola believes his achievements with Portugal should be recognised
articles.content:
Cristiano Ronaldo deserves proper Portugal send-off, says former rival Pep Guardiola

Cristiano Ronaldo walked away from international football earlier this month but Pep Guardiola believes his achievements with Portugal should be recognised

Last Update:

Cristiano Ronaldo deserves to “feel the love of his countrymen” and close the door on his Portugal chapter with a fitting farewell, says Pep Guardiola.

Ronaldo retired from international football earlier this month, due in part to a row with national team boss Jorge Jesus, who left him out of the team to face Norway in a Nations League clash.

The 41-year-old left the squad ahead of the subsequent game with Denmark and then decided to walk away for good. Ronaldo, who continues to play for Saudi Pro League side Al-Nassr, made 234 appearances for Portugal, scoring 146 goals.

The departure was unbefitting for a man who helped Portugal win Euro 2016 and the Nations League titles in 2019 and 2025.

The Portuguese Football Federation have outlined their intention to mark Ronaldo’s contribution with a tribute and Guardiola is adamant that has to happen, to enable both parties to move on.

He told @romariotv_oficial: “The Portuguese Football Federation must ensure a dignified end to Cristiano Ronaldo’s career. Both sides need to make a clear effort to guarantee a farewell as a legend deserves.

“Cristiano Ronaldo shouldn’t leave the Portuguese national team this way. Portugal can’t let him go like this after their story.

“He’s been an incredibly important figure, not only for himself or Portugal but for future generations of Portuguese players.

“They must understand that Cristiano Ronaldo deserves to leave on his own terms. There are exceptional players in your history and Cristiano Ronaldo is one of them; therefore, this situation must be rectified to give Cristiano what he deserves.”

Ronaldo needs to ‘turn the page on the past’ – Guardiola

Guardiola, who had some epic battles with Ronaldo’s Real Madrid when he was in charge of Barcelona, also believes it is important for the striker to get the chance to say a proper farewell and close the book on a hugely important part of his brilliant career.

He added: “Whether they rectify it or not isn’t my concern, but it’s clear honestly in my view that they absolutely must rectify this.

“There should be a celebration where he feels the love of his countrymen, and he, in turn, must also take the initiative and say: let’s turn the page on the past.

“An entire career shouldn’t be judged based on a month or two, or because of a disagreement or misunderstanding with one or two individuals.

“There are careers filled with achievements that deserve to be preserved and defended — Cristiano Ronaldo deserves that.

“There are great players, those who were truly at the pinnacle of their game, who deserve to leave through the front door.

“Firstly, because they earned it through everything they gave to the sport; football itself owes them this clear recognition.”

Ronaldo scored his 987th career goal last night as Al-Nassr edged out Al-Sadd 2-1 in the AFC Champions League elite.

Tip of the Day: United to hit goal trail and wins for PSG and Atletico

Wednesday's Tip of the Day is a Champions League treble

Last Update:

Tuesday’s Tip of the Day was a success, we hope you were on it!

For today, we are delving into the Champions League and have identified a treble we believe will keep the run going.

First up, we have Manchester United’s trip to Sporting CP. Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge, at Liverpool on Sunday, was effectively hijacked by the early dismissal of Leny Yoro and the Argentine will be confident of a better outcome in Lisbon.

But the fact is the defensive frailties remain so we think both teams to score is a good bet.

Next up is for Paris Saint-Germain to beat Roma. The Giallorossi are going well in Serie A and sit second having not lost any of their opening 12 games. In Donyell Malen they also have the division’s top scorer.

They face a PSG side that is without injured duo Khvicha Kvaratskhelia and Desire Doue for the long-term. But Luis Enrique’s men have quality over the field and can still boast a front three that includes 2025 Ballon d’Or winner Ousmane Dembele and World Cup final matchwinner Ferran Torres.

articles.title: Former Al-Nassr star says Cristiano Ronaldo is a ‘problem’ and his obsession with 1,000 goals is holding team back
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo is holding Al-Nassr back, according to one of the club's former players
articles.content:
Former Al-Nassr star says Cristiano Ronaldo is a ‘problem’ and his obsession with 1,000 goals is holding team back

Cristiano Ronaldo is holding Al-Nassr back, according to one of the club's former players

Last Update:

Former Al-Nassr defender Hussein Abdulghani says Cristiano Ronaldo is a “problem” for the Saudi Pro League champions and questioned his value to the team.

Abdulghani, who won two league titles with the club between 2013 and 2015, believes the 41-year-old is becoming a burden for Ange Postecoglou’s side, particularly as he nears 1,000 career goals.

Ronaldo scored number 987 from the penalty spot last night as Al-Nassr edged out Al-Sadd 2-1 in their AFC Champions League Elite clash.

Speaking before the Al-Sadd game, Abdulghani told MBC1: “Everyone knows what Al-Nassr’s problem is, but they pretend they don’t see it. Everyone agrees that Ronaldo was a great player, but let’s leave that aside. The question is: is he a useful player for the team right now, especially in the most balanced of games?

“Scoring goals is not the only function of a forward, there are others. He can’t score a goal and then be a hole in the team for the rest of the game. We are talking in technical terms. Ronaldo is a great player, but he can no longer make a difference. Al-Nassr needs a forward with individual solutions, and not someone who is just on the field for the 90 minutes.”

Fans are scared to criticise Ronaldo – Abdulghani

Abdulghani believes the Portuguese’s obsession with reaching four figures is becoming a sideshow.

“Al-Nassr fans are praying that Ronaldo scores his thousand goals and that this matter ends once and for all,” he added. “Nobody says this for fear of Ronaldo’s fans, but he is a harmful player at Al-Nassr.”

Ronaldo recently retired from international football and can now give his sole attention to Al-Nassr’s bid to retain the title.

They are third in the table, two points adrift of leaders Al-Hilal, who also have a game in hand.

Ronaldo has scored eight goals in 11 league games this season.

articles.title: Ange Postecoglou sets sights on Al-Nassr quadruple: ‘I want to win them all’
articles.summary: Ange Postecoglou has set his sights on all four trophies for Al-Nassr after another win.
articles.content:
Ange Postecoglou sets sights on Al-Nassr quadruple: ‘I want to win them all’

Ange Postecoglou has set his sights on all four trophies for Al-Nassr after another win.

Last Update:

Ange Postecoglou has outlined his ambitions to win four trophies this season, insisting Al-Nassr are capable of competing on all fronts after another win in the AFC Champions League on Tuesday.

The Australian has never been one to shy away from setting ambitious targets and has made it clear that he does not intend to prioritise one competition over another.

Speaking about his ambitions for the remainder of the campaign following a 2-1 win over Al-Saad, Postecoglou insisted he wants his players to challenge for every trophy available to them.

“We have four trophies ahead of us and I want to win them all,” he said.

“We have four competitions ahead of us, and our ambition is to win them all.

“We have a small squad, but the available players are capable of competing.

“We are working on developing young players, like Saad, and this is a positive thing for the team,” he added.

articles.title: Tottenham teenager Williams-Barnett signs new contract
articles.summary: Tottenham youngster Luca Williams-Barnett scored one and made one on his first Premier League start against Ipswich at the weekend
articles.content:
Tottenham teenager Williams-Barnett signs new contract

Tottenham youngster Luca Williams-Barnett scored one and made one on his first Premier League start against Ipswich at the weekend

Last Update:

Tottenham have announced 18-year-old winger Luca Williams-Barnett has signed a new contract.

The academy product has penned fresh terms after bursting on to the scene this season, capped by his first Premier League start against Ipswich at the weekend in which he scored and assisted in a 2-0 win.

Barnett-Williams told the club’s official website: “This is a special moment for me and my family, and one I have worked really hard to reach. But this is only the start.

“Spurs is a family to me. I’ve been here for so long – it’s a second home, where I trust the people and coaches who have pushed me to become the player I am today.

“The club has trusted and believed in me, now I’m ready to repay that.”

De Zerbi delighted Williams-Barnett has committed to Tottenham

England Under-19 international Williams-Barnett, who has been at Spurs since the age of 10, made his Premier League debut off the bench against Crystal Palace last month and also came on in the defeat at Leeds prior to the international break.

Tottenham boss Roberto De Zerbi said: “Luca is a player I think the world of, and I’m so happy that he has signed a new contract.

“He has benefitted from being around the first team every day, growing in stature and consistency, and has deserved his place in the matchday squad over recent weeks.

“Everyone can see how technically gifted Luca is on the pitch but I also love his calmness and decision-making under pressure.

“The best players have confidence on the pitch and humility off it. There is still plenty of room for Luca to improve, and I know he will continue to work hard every day to be the best version of himself.”

Lange hails work of Tottenham academy in nurturing Williams-Barnett

Sporting director Johan Lange added: “We are delighted that Luca has committed his future to the club.

“He is a special talent, whose hard work and mentality has seen him continue to improve at every stage of his development. He fully deserves this new contract.

“Luca’s progression through the academy to this point is a great example of what our pathway is designed to achieve and what is possible for young players here. It is also important to recognise not only the coaches but also the wider academy staff who have supported Luca and played a role in his journey to this point.

“We are excited to watch Luca continue to develop and be an important player for the club, both in the present and the future.”

articles.title: BREAKING: Manchester United win Leny Yoro appeal against red card
articles.summary: Manchester United defender Leny Yoro was sent off early on against Liverpool on Sunday
articles.content:
BREAKING: Manchester United win Leny Yoro appeal against red card

Manchester United defender Leny Yoro was sent off early on against Liverpool on Sunday

Last Update:

Leny Yoro’s red card against Liverpool has been overturned after Manchester United appealed the decision.

Yoro was dismissed just eight minutes into Sunday’s game for bringing down Alexander Isak when the Sweden striker bore down on goal.

Referee Sam Barrott showed Yoro the red card for denying an obvious goalscoring opportunity, meaning United had to play the remainder of Mauricio Pochettino’s debut game in charge with 10 men.

Pochettino argued afterwards that Isak had lost control of the ball and it would’ve been gathered by the outrushing United goalkeeper Senne Lammens and that was the verdict of the independent regulatory commission.

The Argentine said: “I don’t agree because the ball wasn’t in Isak’s control. Leny was running with him and when Isak saw the control wasn’t good and the ball was going to the keeper it is normal you delay, you stop running, and you wait to feel the touch and you go down. It is never a foul.”

United wilt after Yoro red

Liverpool took full advantage of the extra man and cruised to a 4-0 win.

Dominik Szoboszlai fired home the free-kick awarded for Yoro’s foul and a clever Florian Wirtz volley meant it was 2-0 shortly afterwards. Second-half goals from Rio Ngumoha and Victor Muñoz capped a thoroughly miserable afternoon for United.

Yoro had been due to miss Saturday’s home game with Brentford as a result of the one-match ban but he will now be available as United look to clamber out of the relegation zone.

The 21-year-old is likely to start when United go to Sporting CP in the Champions League on Wednesday night.

articles.title: AFCON 2025: Senegal awarded trophy after CAS appeal
articles.summary: Senegal's appeal was successful and they have been handed the trophy
articles.content:
AFCON 2025: Senegal awarded trophy after CAS appeal

Senegal's appeal was successful and they have been handed the trophy

Last Update:

Senegal have been awarded the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations title by the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS).

The Lions of Teranga were controversially stripped of the crown by the Confederation of African Football (CAF) in March and the trophy handed to Morocco. Senegal appealed to CAS and a three-man panel today ruled in their favour.

Senegal beat Morocco 1-0 after extra time in the final on January 18, with Pape Gueye scoring the decisive goal.

However, that came following remarkable scenes that saw Senegal refuse to play after the tournament hosts were awarded a highly contentious penalty in stoppage time.

After a delay of around 17 minutes, Senegal’s players returned to the pitch, and Brahim Diaz’s ill-advised panenka was saved, forcing the extra period in which Gueye struck.

Senegal joy turns to anger

The jubilation of their triumph turned to fury two months later.

An initial disciplinary hearing had seen CAF hand down a series of fines and bans for Senegal and Morocco players and officials, but the result was allowed to stand.

But African football’s governing body then subsequently ruled that Senegal were “declared to have forfeited the final match” with the “result of the match being recorded as 3-0 in favour” of Morocco.

Senegal unsurprisingly elected to take the case to CAS, sport’s highest court, which elected against an expedited procedure.

Restarting the match key to Senegal’s court victory

Senegal insisted the game had not been “forfeited” as it continued into extra-time, and CAS agreed with that assessment.

The key part of the CAS statement released on Tuesday read: “AFCON Regulations are intended solely to determine the outcome of a match when a team’s conduct leads the referee to call off the game permanently, they are therefore not applicable in this case … Panel considers that in resuming the match, the Referee did not err in law.”

Senegal endured disappointment at this year’s World Cup, as they were knocked out in the last 32 after progressing through the group stage as one of the eight best third-placed teams.

They were eliminated at hands of Belgium, surrendering a 2-0 lead to lose 3-2 after extra time, with that exit seeing coach Pape Thiaw sacked. Morocco were knocked out in the quarter-finals by France.

articles.title: Fofana talked out of retirement because he has ‘so much money left to take’ from Chelsea
articles.summary: Wesley Fofana has done his reputation no good by laughing off his penalty miss at Liverpool earlier in the season and outlining how much money he still has to claim at Chelsea
articles.content:
Fofana talked out of retirement because he has ‘so much money left to take’ from Chelsea

Wesley Fofana has done his reputation no good by laughing off his penalty miss at Liverpool earlier in the season and outlining how much money he still has to claim at Chelsea

Last Update:

Chelsea defender Wesley Fofana had to be talked out of retiring by his agents and reminded “how much money he still has to take” from the club.

The French centre-half has endured a rough time with injuries after joining Chelsea from Leicester for an initial £70million in August 2022, making just 61 Premier League appearances in over four seasons.

The 25-year-old admitted they had taken a toll but when he raised the prospect of retiring, he was quickly talked out of it given he still has two-and-a-half years left of a seven-year deal worth a reported £200,000 a week.

“I was truly convinced that I was going to get hurt again,” Fofana said in an interview with Zack Nani TV.

“I thought, ‘That’s it.’ I thought I was Abou Diaby. I thought it was my destiny, I will accept it. I was disgusted because it’s my dream. I thought I was Abou Diaby.

“I sat with my agents, and I said, ‘I’m stopping football.’ After they spoke to me about my contract et cetera, they told me it was simple, ‘You have so many years of contract, you still have so much money left to take, even if you stop playing football, you’ll show up, put a smile on your face even if you stayed injured, you have a contract you have to finish, for your future.’”

Fofana laughs off spot-kick woe that cost Chelsea at Liverpool

Fofana has struggled for form as well as fitness this season and has played seven times in the league for a Chelsea team that have slipped to eighth in the table after losing three of their last four games.

They are also out of the EFL Cup after Fofana’s miss in a penalty shoot-out saw them lose at Liverpool.

It was another major blow for boss Xabi Alonso but Fofana says he can laugh about it now.

“I’ve experienced things,” added Fofana. “If I miss it’s not serious, it’s definitely annoying, but if someone attacks me, it’s not the first time, I don’t care. I know there’s another match in three days.

“If you win, you forget about your penalty. It’s how football works. I missed. I had a beautiful shot, did you see it? I was shooting very high. The roof of Anfield.

“I remember a supporter very high up caught the ball. Yeah, I missed, now I laugh about it because it’s part of football. That’s how it is.”

Carragher blasts troubled Chelsea defender Fofana

Fofana has also had his issues off the field this year and is currently serving an 18-month driving ban for speeding down the hard shoulder of the A3 in his Lamborghini in April.

His recent performances were discussed by former Liverpool defender Jamie Carragher on Monday Night Football.

Carragher feels Chelsea have “no chance of achieving anything” with Fofana and Levi Colwill at centre-half.

He said: “Chelsea have got a massive problem at centre-back and if they don’t change it in January, they’re going to have a big problem in terms of where they feel they should be this season with the Champions League.

“Until they sign that dominant centre-back and leader, they’ve got absolutely no chance of achieving anything.

“Colwill at Sunderland against [Brian] Brobbey gave the penalty away, and the manager took him off at half-time.

“Fofana’s performance against Manchester United, especially in the first half, was one of the worst you’ll see from a centre-back this season.

“As a partnership, this will never work because they’re not physical enough and there’s no real leader there.”

Chelsea return to league action on Friday night when they visit Nottingham Forest.

articles.title: It doesn’t get any harder than facing Man United, says Sporting CP star Guilherme (and we don’t think he was joking)
articles.summary: Manchester United are in crisis but they are still a name to be feared in Europe, according to Sporting CP forward Luis Guilherme
articles.content:
It doesn’t get any harder than facing Man United, says Sporting CP star Guilherme (and we don’t think he was joking)

Manchester United are in crisis but they are still a name to be feared in Europe, according to Sporting CP forward Luis Guilherme

Last Update:

Sporting CP forward Luis Guilherme says “it does not get any harder” than facing Manchester United.

The teams clash in the Champions League on Wednesday night with Guilherme’s words coming as a surprise to anyone who has watched United recently.

They sit second from bottom of the Premier League table and were hammered 4-0 by arch rivals Liverpool on Sunday in new boss Mauricio Pochettino’s first game in charge.

Things have been slightly better in the Champions League and United head to Portugal in 17th position in the league phase with two wins and two defeats from their four matches.

The club appear to have hit rock bottom, at least domestically, but Guilherme insists it will be a very difficult game for the hosts at the Estadio Jose Alvalade.

The Brazilian said: “It doesn’t get any harder than this. We’re talking about a huge club, not just in England but the wider world. They now have a different coach, so they’ll want to prove a point. They’re not in good form, but they’ll want to show the grandeur of their club and to try and surprise, but we’ll prepare as best as we can to get the win.”

United look on in envy at Fonseca effect

Sporting also have a new manager in Paulo Fonseca but they have enjoyed a bounce with the former AC Milan boss winning both of his first two games.

Guilherme added: ”He’s a father figure but also makes you train hard, and makes you work when you have to. However, he’s always open for a chat when there’s time to do so. He’s always sharing his experiences. Before he was appointed, I asked Endrick what he was like as a coach. He played under him at Lyon, and he speaks highly of him.

“We’ve only been working together for a few weeks, but the short amount of time we’ve had together has given us an idea of his plans. Now it’s about implementing them in training during the international break. I think we’re on the up.”

articles.title: Champions League predictions: Joy for Arsenal, Man City and Liverpool but more frustration for Pochettino’s United
articles.summary: Europe could provide some respite for the Manchester clubs while Arsenal and Aston Villa will also look for morale-boosting wins. Here are our Champions League predictions...
articles.content:
Champions League predictions: Joy for Arsenal, Man City and Liverpool but more frustration for Pochettino’s United

Europe could provide some respite for the Manchester clubs while Arsenal and Aston Villa will also look for morale-boosting wins. Here are our Champions League predictions...

Last Update:

The Champions League is back this week and the two Manchester clubs are hoping Europe will provide a little respite from their domestic struggles.

City have now gone four Premier League games without a win following the weekend draw with Fulham while United’s plight is even more desperate with new boss Mauricio Pochettino suffering a miserable first game in charge at Liverpool.

Arsenal and Aston Villa were also held over the weekend.

Here are this week’s games and our predictions for the stand-out fixtures.

TUESDAY

Galatasaray v Aston Villa (5.45pm)Villa return to Istanbul, the scene of their Europa League triumph in May, but they head to Turkey on the back of a frustrating goalless draw at home to Sunderland on Saturday. Unai Emery’s men are without a win since their 2-1 defeat of Manchester City on October 24 – a run of five games – and will need be at their best against a Gala side that have won their last eight in all competitions. The hosts are three points clear at the top of the Super Lig and also enjoyed Champions League wins over Lille and Stuttgart. There have been concerns about the pitch at RAMS Park and that will add a layer of intrigue to what should be an open game.Prediction: Galatasaray 3-2 Aston Villa

Arsenal v Borussia Dortmund (8pm)Arsenal will feel it was two points dropped in a 2-2 draw at Newcastle on Saturday evening but it was another performance in which they didn’t quite hit top gear. That has been a recurring theme this season even though Mikel Arteta’s side sit six points clear at the top of the Premier League. Dortmund are top of the Bundesliga and appear set to provide Bayern Munich with a legitimate title challenge this season. Niko Kovac’s side have yet to lose domestically and are also going well in Europe with three wins from four games.Prediction: Arsenal 2-1 Borussia Dortmund

Manchester City v Napoli (8pm)City’s recent struggles have come as a surprise given the blistering start they made under Enzo Maresca. The Italian denies it but it seems the uncertainty surrounding their possible sanction for breaching financial regulations has had an effect on the squad. They will hope the distraction of European football will prove beneficial against a Napoli squad without several key players due to injury. The visitors still possess plenty of names familiar to an English audience, though, including Kevin De Bruyne, who will return to the Etihad, and former United man Scott McTominay.Prediction: Manchester City 3-1 Napoli

Real Madrid v PSV Eindhoven (8pm)Jose Mourinho’s Madrid side registered their ninth successive win at the weekend, although they were made to work hard for it by Celta Vigo. The 15-time winners are one of just two clubs – defending champions PSG being the other – with a 100% record after four games and it would be a major surprise if they didn’t extend that record in this one. PSV are top of the Eredivisie but have won just once in Europe. This would appear a step up in class that could prove problematic.Prediction: Real Madrid 5-0 PSV Eindhoven

UEFA Champions League

– League Stage – 5

Tuesday 24, November 2026

Wednesday 25, November 2026

WEDNESDAY

Sabah v Barcelona (5.45pm)Barcelona head to Azerbaijan without the injured Lamine Yamal but still riding the wave of Sunday’s thrilling 3-2 defeat of Villarreal. Hansi Flick’s men lead La Liga and are ticking over nicely in the Champions League as well, yet doubts remain as to the quality of their defending against the elite teams. The trip to Baku won’t provide any answers on that debate with Barca likely to dominate the ball. Sabah have, understandably, found the going tough in the Champions League but they still harbour hopes of squeezing into the play-off spots thanks to the win over Slavia Prague.Prediction: Sabah 0-3 Barcelona

Club Brugge v Liverpool (8pm)Liverpool finally clicked against Manchester United although they were undoubtedly helped by playing against 10 men for the majority of a one-sided encounter. Andoni Iraola’s men have had mixed results on the road in the Champions League this season, hammering LASK 6-3 before going down 3-2 at Fenerbahce. This is a tricky assignment with the Belgian side going surprisingly well with three wins from four games.Prediction: Club Brugge 1-2 Liverpool

Sporting CP v Manchester United (8pm)The Champions League is almost an afterthought for United given their issues domestically. This squad has no chance of winning Europe’s elite club competition and their man focus is avoiding relegation to the Championship. Pochettino will relish the chance to spend some time with his players following his whirlwind introduction last week and he will need to get to work on the training pitch to iron out their many flaws. Sporting are going well in Europe with three wins from four but have not set the world alight in the Primeira Liga and currently sit third behind FC Porto and Benfica.Prediction: Sporting CP 1-1 Manchester United

articles.content:
Tip of the Day: Ignore the Champions League and focus on this EFL double

We have identified two EFL games to make up our Tip of the Day...

Last Update:

Monday’s Tip of the Day was undermined by the early red card to Everton’s James Tarkowski but we go again!

Today’s predictions come from the EFL as there doesn’t appear a lot of value in tonight’s Champions League offering.

So, we have identified two games that we feel can prove beneficial.

The first is the Championship clash between Sheffield United and Southampton at Bramall Lane. Both sides are going well with the Blades recovering from a slow start to the season and a run of four wins from six games has seen them move up the table.

They have scored eight goals in their last three outings and hammered Watford 4-0 at the weekend.

Southampton are among the favourites to go up and start the night inside the play-off positions. They have won five of their last eight and are the fourth-highest scorers in the second tier with 31 goals in 16 games.

We fancy both teams to get on the scoresheet in what should be a good game.

The second leg comes just down the road in Bradford with Yorkshire rivals Barnsley the visitors.

Barnsley have struggled this season with Daniel Stendel’s young team propping up the division. They have lost eight of their last 10 in the league and not won since early September.

They go to a Bradford side that have lost one of their last 16 in all competitions.

Tuesday’s Tip of the Day (all odds are from bet365 and correct as of 0930am GMT on Tuesday, November 24)

articles.title: FIFA confirms 2035 Women’s World Cup will be held in UK for first time
articles.summary: The UK has never previously hosted the tournament.
articles.content:
FIFA confirms 2035 Women’s World Cup will be held in UK for first time

The UK has never previously hosted the tournament.

Last Update:

FIFA has confirmed the 2035 Women’s World Cup will be held in the United Kingdom.

The tournament, which was first held in 1991, has never been staged on British soil before. However, that is set to change, with matches to be held in England, Wales, Scotland and Northern Ireland in 2035.

There were no rival bids to stage the competition, which will be the second to feature 48 teams, with expansion coming into effect for the 2031 Women’s World Cup.

A joint statement from the chief executives of the four UK football associations — Mark Bullingham (The FA), Patrick Nelson (Irish FA), Ian Maxwell (Scottish FA) and Noel Mooney (FAW) read: “Hosting the FIFA Women’s World Cup 2035 is a landmark moment for England, Scotland, Northern Ireland and Wales.

“We are grateful to FIFA’s member associations for the trust placed in our four associations today.

“‘All Together’ has been our vision from the first day of this bid, and it is how we intend to host. One tournament, hosted across four nations, with a legacy that reaches well beyond them.

“What follows now is eight and a half years of work; on facilities, on coaching, on officiating, on the pathways that take a girl from her first game to a professional contract. The players who will light up 2035 are in our parks and playgrounds right now.

“A tournament of this scale is an opportunity for the whole of the women’s game, and we want its benefits felt in the places that need them most.

‘We look forward to welcoming the world in 2035.”

The 2031 edition will be held in United States, Mexico, Costa Rica and Jamaica after those four countries combined to submit the sole bid for the tournament.

Four-time winners USA have hosted the tournament three times twice previously, doing so in 1999 and 2003.

articles.title: Relief for Arteta and Arsenal as Raya avoids surgery on injured arm
articles.summary: David Raya will not undergo surgery on the arm injury he sustained at Newcastle on Saturday, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said today
articles.content:
Relief for Arteta and Arsenal as Raya avoids surgery on injured arm

David Raya will not undergo surgery on the arm injury he sustained at Newcastle on Saturday, Arsenal boss Mikel Arteta said today

Last Update:

Mikel Arteta has outlined his relief that Arsenal goalkeeper David Raya has not suffered a serious injury, although he will miss Tuesday night’s Champions League game with Borussia Dortmund.

The Spain goalkeeper hurt his arm during Saturday’s 2-2 draw with Newcastle, triggering fears he may require surgery.

But Arteta revealed the issue had settled quite quickly, although the club will know more tomorrow after further tests.

He said: ”He is not fit for tomorrow unfortunately but it doesn’t look too serious. We need some more tests but it is quite encouraging with the pain that he was showing immediately after the action – we were all quite worried but it seems to be better than what we expected.

“When you look at the action it doesn’t seem to be much but the extent of the pain that he had and how he was struggling, it was quite worrying. He does not need to have surgery which was the worry as that would rule him out for months so let’s see.”

Kepa likely to start in goal for Arsenal against Dortmund

Raya is arguably Arsenal’s most important player following a string of brilliant performances since joining from Brentford, initially on loan, three years ago. His injury means either Kepa Arrizabalaga or Illan Meslier will start in goal against Dortmund. The hope is Raya will be ready to return for Sunday’s game with Manchester City.

Arteta added: ”We have seen what David brings to the team but as well that is why we are very protective with Kepa and Illan and everybody needs to be ready because these things unfortunately happen and now we need to show everyone how well we are protected and the good keepers that we have in Kepa and Illan.”

France defender William Saliba may see some minutes tomorrow after being named on the bench for the game at St James’ Park.

“There are other steps obviously because of the amount of time he has trained with us right now,” said Arteta. “The competitive level is what it is but now we talk about playing against the top teams in the Premier League and Champions League and that is a completely new world. The player needs exposure and we will find the right moments to do that.”

Noni Madueke grabbed Arsenal’s equaliser at the weekend and Arteta has been pleased with his performances in place of the injured Bukayo Saka.

“He is becoming decisive in games and that is what we need from players,” he said “He is adding variety and much more connection within his games, rather than rely everything on one-to-one actions.

“I love his intensity without the ball so he is becoming a much more complete player I would say and I think he is enjoying this a lot.”

Arsenal boss wary of Dortmund threat

Arsenal go into the game in third place in the Champions League table having taken 10 points from their first four matches. And Arteta concedes he enjoys the new league phase format even if it does mean more work.

He added: “It’s much more work than it used to be because you have to analyse many more opponents. You test yourself constantly against top competition and not only for us but there are some incredible games to watch. I think it has created more uncertainty probably, more openness and urgency that every game you need the urgency to win it. Every opponent is so tough.”

Dortmund will arrive in North London in confident mood. They are top of the Bundesliga and have yet to lose in the German top flight.

“I am very impressed with them and you see their results so far, where they are in the Bundesliga and where they are in the Champions League – the way they are playing, they way they are dominating games,” he said. “We had them here in pre-season and they showed their quality and what they are capable of so we are very much aware of that but we will play at home in front of our crowd and go and attack the game, that’s for sure.”

articles.title: Jose Mourinho says Arda Guler and Jude Bellingham are two of the ‘good liars’ in his Real Madrid squad
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho was impressed by his Real Madrid team's never-say-die attitude in the win over Celta Vigo on Saturday, even if he was misled by some of his players
articles.content:
Jose Mourinho says Arda Guler and Jude Bellingham are two of the ‘good liars’ in his Real Madrid squad

Jose Mourinho was impressed by his Real Madrid team's never-say-die attitude in the win over Celta Vigo on Saturday, even if he was misled by some of his players

Last Update:

Jose Mourinho hailed his “good liars” as his jaded Real Madrid squad prepared to face PSV Eindhoven in the Champions League on Tuesday night.

Madrid eked out a 2-1 victory over Celta Vigo on Saturday – Carlos Espi grabbing a late winner – to remain in second place in La Liga, three points behind Barcelona.

The fixture came at the end of another exhausting international break with most of the squad travelling around the world to play for their countries.

Mourinho admitted some of his players may have told a few untruths in order to play, but says sometimes it is necessary.

Asked if he was worried by Madrid’s recent need to win late – they also grabbed an injury-time goal to steal all three points at AEK Athens in their last Champions League outing – Mourinho had mixed feelings.

He said: “It depends on the situation. Winning in the last minute has many good things but also has its risks. In the last 15 minutes [against Celta Vigo], the risk was there. When you risk it and change the profile and go for everything, you open the door so that you can have a setback and not get a single point. And you can lose.

“The perfect situation is a game like Valencia, like Santander. Within five minutes you know how the game will end. There are others in which you are not capable of doing that. I said that Celta would be a complicated game.

“The situation of traveling, of not training, of being together for the first time the day before… Luckily I have good liars, those who tell me they are fit to play, and they are not. I love them, but they tell me they’re ready and they’re not.

“With these factors there is a borderline situation. You think it’s fantastic, but if we think about the last minutes [against Celta]…playing with Arda [Guler] and Jude [Bellingham], both dead, but playing with a lot of mentality.

“In normal conditions you don’t win those games. They are gold points. Credit to everyone, also to the liars who have given everything.”

Vinicius Jr to return to Real Madrid starting XI

Mourinho seems likely to rotate against PSV given the physical demands on his players and that will mean a return to the starting XI for Vinicius Jr, who started the Celta game on the bench.

The 26-year-old Brazil winger has had a poor start to the season but came alive in the two games over the international break, scoring five times against Japan and Singapore.

“He will return to his maximum potential,” said Mourinho. “He is young, sometimes players when they approach 30 or 32 cannot maintain the ideal physical level. There are players who lose motivation a little when they reach those ages. Vini is young. People forget that he arrived here very young and that perhaps he reached a very high level too soon.

“This weekend it went well, he helped to change the game. Tomorrow he will play and we expect his best version. I’ve known his best version, but I was on the other side. Benfica dominating, the Bernabéu quiet… Vinicius’ goal and the tie is over. It’s the Vini we want. But there is no pressure on my part. He must help offensively, also defensively to balance.”

Real Madrid boss wary of experienced PSV

PSV are top of the Eredivisie but have found the going harder in Europe with one win from four matches.

It seems a straightforward game for Madrid but Mourinho was quick to point out how tough it will be.

He said: “They are a good team, a team that is worth more than the points it has. They don’t come here to think about losing. They are a good team with good players and an experienced coach in Peter Bosz.

“Players like Filip Kostic, Ivan Perisic, years of European experience. It’s not easy. Three days between games is fine, two days is hard. It has to be that way, but it’s hard. They also played on Saturday but it was easier for them as they were 4-0 up after 60 minutes. Fresh legs with energy will help us.”

articles.title: ‘We’re at our lowest point and no-one is coming to save us’ – Mainoo outlines desperation at Man United following Liverpool hammering
articles.summary: Manchester United were dreadful in losing 4-0 at Liverpool yesterday
articles.content:
‘We’re at our lowest point and no-one is coming to save us’ – Mainoo outlines desperation at Man United following Liverpool hammering

Manchester United were dreadful in losing 4-0 at Liverpool yesterday

Last Update:

Manchester United midfielder Kobbie Mainoo says the club are at their lowest ebb and “no-one is coming to save us”.

The feelgood factor that surrounded Mauricio Pochettino’s arrival lasted barely 10 minutes at Liverpool yesterday with the dismissal of Leny Yoro and Dominik Szoboszlai’s free-kick paving the way for a 4-0 drubbing that left United mired in 19th place in the Premier League table.

Florian Wirtz, Rio Ngumoha and Victor Munoz were also on target as United endured an afternoon to forget on Merseyside.

Mainoo was taken off with three minutes to go but was a peripheral figure throughout as United struggled to cope with 10 men in the face of a superb Liverpool display.

And afterwards he gave a downbeat assessment of United’s current mindset.

He told MUTV: “It’s all about character now. We’re at the lowest we’ve ever been and no one’s coming to save us. There’s no helping hands coming so we’ve got to work together and lean on each other and keep working and hopefully it’ll come good.

“It is a tough place to come, but I can’t fault the boys on their fight. We have to take the pain from the game and move on with it.”

We are committed – Mainoo insists squad is united

United have claimed eight points from their opening 11 games and only sit above rock-bottom Crystal Palace in the table.

They go to Sporting CP in the Champions League in midweek.

Mainoo added: “The games are still coming thick and fast, so we don’t have time to dwell on it.

“We’re all committed. No-one is going anywhere and we’re all leaning on each other.

“We all know what we have to do and we all know with the new manager we need to get behind him, keep working in training. That’s all we can do.”

After the trip to Portugal, United face crunch Premier League games against Brentford, Newcastle and Coventry.

Pochettino will be expected to claim a decent points haul from those fixtures, and the Argentine opted not to go heavy on his players following the Anfield debacle and cited Yoro’s early dismissal as mitigation.

He said: ”What I learned from my players 25th November 2026 is that they like to fight. They are committed with the team, with the club, and of course they want to win games.

“Today we made an unbelievable effort. Today was a test. After eight minutes, 10 men, red card, concede the goal in this action. Do you think that is easy?

“Even the best team in the world playing like this in this situation, in our circumstance, maybe concede the four goals or maybe more.”

Keane hammers woeful United

Others were less charitable.

Former United skipper Roy Keane, watching from the Sky Sports studio, could not believe how bad United had been against their greatest rivals and disagreed with commentator Gary Neville, who felt the scoreline was respectable given the circumstances.

“If I hear that one more time from the lads in the commentary that 4-0 is not too bad when you’re down to 10 men – has a team ever got a result with 10 men before?” Keane said. “It can be done.

“I thought United were desperate. [The red card] doesn’t help but you’re telling me they couldn’t have done better? They lost 4-0 with 10 men, that’s not too bad? Has a team ever got a result with 10 men? It can be done. At least show a bit more fight, a bit more quality – I can’t believe what I’m hearing from people.

“You played for the club, saying 4-0 isn’t too bad. Wow. Fans are applauding. Applauding what? Performing rubbish. Liverpool were excellent, but how easy did United make it for them? I can’t believe what I’m watching sometimes.

“This team two years ago finished 15th. The last year or two, we’re talking. We’re blaming the board, blaming ownership, blaming managers.

“When do the players take responsibility for some decision-making? Liverpool probably should have scored eight, probably eight or nine, unbelievable chances they had. And everyone’s coming off the pitch saying four is not too bad? I feel like swearing.”

articles.title: Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal to miss midweek Champions League game due to ankle injury
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal will sit out Barcelona's game with Sabah on Wednesday night but should be back for the weekend game against Deportivo La Coruna
articles.content:
Barcelona winger Lamine Yamal to miss midweek Champions League game due to ankle injury

Lamine Yamal will sit out Barcelona's game with Sabah on Wednesday night but should be back for the weekend game against Deportivo La Coruna

Last Update:

Barcelona have announced Lamine Yamal will miss Wednesday night’s Champions League game with Sabah due to a minor ankle injury.

The 19-year-old played the full 90 minutes as Barca hit back from 2-0 down to beat Villarreal on Sunday but is suffering from what the club have described as “mild discomfort in his right ankle” and will sit out the midweek game as a result.

Yamal is expected to return for Sunday’s trip to Deportivo La Coruna.

A club statement read: “First-team player Lamine Yamal is experiencing mild discomfort in his right ankle. As a precaution, he will miss the match against Sabah and is expected to be available for next Sunday’s match against Deportivo.”

Barcelona head to Baku in fifth place in the Champions League table to face the Azerbaijan side who are 31st.

It is, therefore, a good time to rest the teenager, who sat out Spain’s trip to Czechia during the international break because of a knee injury.

Yamal also missed the end of last season after sustaining a serious hamstring problem but returned in time to help Spain win the World Cup.

Yamal plays key role as Barcelona hit back to stun Villarreal

He had an eventful afternoon against Villarreal, although there were signs he was not fully fit in the warm-up when he received attention from the medical staff.

That did not stop him from playing a full role against the Yellow Submarine.

After missing a first-half penalty, Yamal then laid on the equaliser for Fermin Lopez with a run and slide-rule pass across the area.

He was also instrumental in the winner with a clever flick that enabled Eric Garcia to cross and defender Pau Navarro to prod the ball into his own net.

The win enabled Hansi Flick’s side to restore their three-point lead at the top of La Liga over Real Madrid, who also came from behind to see off Celta Vigo on Saturday night.

articles.content:
Pochettino tells United to ‘care more about everything’ after ‘painful’ defeat

United have the second-worst defensive record in the Premier League

Last Update:

Mauricio Pochettino has told Manchester United to “translate that anger to an energy” after his first game in charge ended in a 4-0 defeat at Liverpool in the Premier League.

Five days after Pochettino succeeded the sacked Michael Carrick, second-bottom United lost Leny Yoro to a straight red card after eight minutes and were 2-0 behind five minutes later as their winless domestic run extended to 10 matches.

“When a situation is like this, to turn a negative to a positive we need to make double the effort,” said Pochettino (via United’s website), describing Yoro’s dismissal for impeding Alexander Isak as the last defender “a difficult decision that we maybe don’t agree with”.

“More concentration, more focus, care more about everything. Yesterday, someone said to me that a journey of 1,000 miles starts from one step… we need to take [stock] after the defeat.”

Liverpool vs Man United ‘painful’

United visit a Sporting side who are three points above them in the Champions League on Wednesday (20:00 GMT), then host opponents who are nine places ahead of them in the Premier League when they face Brentford on Saturday (15:00).

“It’s so painful,” Pochettino rued of the trouncing at Anfield. “We feel pain for the defeat but we need to keep our heads up and translate that anger to an energy, to start to work from [Monday] for the next game.

“It wasn’t a difficult week. We handled the situation [very well] and [our difficulties are] not an excuse. We are here to try to improve all together and be successful.”

United are a point from safety and one above bottom side Crystal Palace.

Manchester United team vs Liverpool

United’s three changes from their 4-4 draw at home to Aston Villa on November 8 featured Matthijs de Ligt making his first league start since November 2025, Lisandro Martinez returning from a one-game ban and Patrick Dorgu’s reinstatement.

articles.content:
Hull hero McBurnie hails ‘horrible’ Tigers after late home win over Brighton

Hull have won two and drawn four of their home games this season

Last Update:

Oli McBurnie says Hull City “rode their luck” after the forward struck twice from close range on the break during second-half added time in the Tigers’ 2-0 home win over Brighton & Hove Albion in the Premier League.

The second-placed Seagulls hit the crossbar through Yasin Ayari’s first-half shot and finished the opening period with an expected goals total of 1.75 to Hull’s 0.2, but McBurnie pounced for a double inside four minutes after opposition full-back Costinha was dismissed in the 89th minute.

“We know if we’re always in games, we fancy ourselves to get chances and make it as horrible as possible,” said McBurnie, who has scored all four of his league goals this season across the last four games for Hull, who ended a nine-match winless run in all competitions.

“We haven’t lost a game at home [this season]. [Brighton are] a top, top team. We knew how tough it was going to be and in the first half we rode our luck. In the second half, we probably did as well.”

Hull vs Brighton: Tzolakis ‘fantastic’

Hull goalkeeper Konstantinos Tzolakis made seven saves. “We’ve got a big man in there,” McBurnie said of the new signing.

“It’s what his job is: to keep the ball out the back of the net. He’s done unbelievably today. We give him a bit a stick about his gear and that, but he’s been good in the net.

“He was fantastic and kept us in the game. That’s how we want to be; [how] we want to play.”

The result moved Hull five points clear of the relegation zone and four behind fourth-placed Bournemouth. City and Brighton are next in action next Sunday (14:05 GMT), when City visit bottom side Crystal Palace and Albion host Newcastle, who will finish this weekend 13th.

articles.title: Flick claims La Liga officials picked on Barcelona during win over Villarreal
articles.summary: Barca and Villarreal each had a player dismissed in La Liga
articles.content:
Flick claims La Liga officials picked on Barcelona during win over Villarreal

Barca and Villarreal each had a player dismissed in La Liga

Last Update:

Hansi Flick says he does not know why Fermin Lopez was dismissed from Barcelona’s technical area during their home win over Villarreal in La Liga, adding that his side have to play “even better” in games refereed by Alejandro Hernandez Hernandez.

Barca recovered from falling 2-0 behind after eight minutes and missing a penalty through Lamine Yamal’s spot kick against a post, winning 3-2 but having Fermin Lopez sent off for dissent following the winger’s substitution in the 68th minute.

“I’m happy with referees in general, but not with this one,” said Flick (via AS), adding that his team should have received a second penalty for a “clear foul” on Yamal.

“The assistants, the fourth official [Alejandro Clemente Ortuno] were constantly watching us. But I always tell the team that if that happens, we have to play even better.

“The job of a fourth official is to support the referee on the field, but he was always looking at our bench. We always have these problems with this referee; it’s happened to us before.”

Barcelona vs Villarreal: La Liga referees ‘always same’

Villarreal midfielder Santi Comesana told a post-match interview that Hernandez had been swayed by Barca’s protests and suggested the reigning champions and Real Madrid have undue influence over officials during matches.

Hernandez, 44, has been a Liga referee since 2012 and gave Fermin Lopez a red card for a second-half foul during Barca’s 4-1 win at Sevilla in La Liga in February 2025.

“I don’t know,” Flick replied when he was asked about Comesana’s comments. “It’s always the same. This season I thought things would be calmer but it seems that’s not the case.

“I asked why I got a yellow card; I didn’t know. It’s a communication issue.”

Villarreal were reduced to 10 players in the 93rd minute when Pau Navarro, whose own-goal decided the contest, received a second booking.

Barcelona team vs Villarreal

Barcelona made three changes from their 2-1 win at Atletico Madrid in La Liga on November 8, bringing in defender Eric Garcia, midfielder Frenkie de Jong and forward Karim Adeyemi.

articles.title: Jose Mourinho points to Arsenal, Chelsea and Man City and says Madrid ‘weren’t 100% focused’
articles.summary: Kylian Mbappe sent Madrid's penalty over against Celta Vigo
articles.content:
Jose Mourinho points to Arsenal, Chelsea and Man City and says Madrid ‘weren’t 100% focused’

Kylian Mbappe sent Madrid's penalty over against Celta Vigo

Last Update:

Real Madrid boss Jose Mourinho says he “immediately” sensed his players had been distracted by the international break before they almost suffered a shock at home to Celta Vigo in La Liga.

Entering on an eight-match winning run in all competitions, Madrid conceded an early opener, missed a first-half penalty through Kylian Mbappe and were deservedly behind until Jude Bellingham struck their equaliser in the 66th minute, with substitute Carlos Espi adding the 85th-minute winner.

“If we look at the big teams that played today and have many international players, Arsenal didn’t win, [Manchester] City didn’t win, Chelsea didn’t win,” argued Mourinho (via AS), also referencing Bayern Munich’s 1-1 draw at home to Koln and Porto’s win on penalties at home to third-tier team Paredes on Friday.

“It’s difficult… these are difficult periods. Today’s points are worth their weight in gold.”

Real Madrid vs Celta Vigo ‘complicated’

Facing opponents who are winless away in this season’s Liga, Madrid struggled for long periods but dominated late on to move level on points at the top with Barcelona, who host ninth-placed Villarreal on Sunday (13:00 GMT).

“Some arrived on Tuesday, others on Wednesday,” Mourinho said of his squad, admitting that he had not expected the contest to be as “difficult” as it proved.

“Others took a 12-hour flight to train on Friday. A situation like this is always complicated. Normally, the ideal thing after a break is to play on Sunday, but that’s not possible because of the Champions League.

“I’ve seen people suffering physically, not at their best. And then there were others who overcame that and found strength in the group – because it’s not an isotonic drink that’s going to give them energy at half-time, but the group of friends.

“[This was] a team that wanted to win and knew how to do it despite the difficulty. And after the second goal, with an unbalanced team, with Arda [Guler] and Jude in the middle, who aren’t midfielders… well, that team knew how to be a team, to work hard.

“I wanted a sixth substitution to take off Kylian or Arda and bring on [Aurelien] Tchouameni, but I didn’t have one. All of this carries risks… if we lose 2-1, we’re talking about a different story.

“That’s why the ideal is to play well from the first minute. We’ve done it many times, but not today: [Ibrahima] Konate passed the ball to the ball boy. And I immediately got the feeling that the players weren’t 100% focused.

“I’m a little frustrated because I want to play better but, at the same time, I’m proud of them, of the group they are and having earned three important points.”

Mourinho was asked about comments he reportedly made to the club’s channel suggesting that his players have to deal with the challenge of losing at home and being booed.

Match Statistics

Mourinho: Booing ‘doesn’t help’ Madrid

Madrid fans made their dissatisfaction audible as their team toiled, with goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois making several saves to stop Celta from doubling their lead.

“I think you understood that I wasn’t criticising the fans,” said Mourinho. “And I never will, because they are sovereign.

“But it’s more difficult. It’s easier to play with support than against your own stadium. If you play away and the fans are hostile, it’s an incentive.

“But playing at home… it’s more complicated, and you have to know how to play under that pressure. It doesn’t help.

“But you have to know how to play. Knowing how to withstand this pressure is also a characteristic of Real Madrid players: to keep going, not being afraid to take risks. And they have shown that strength.”

Real Madrid team vs Celta Vigo

Trent Alexander-Arnold, Eduardo Camavinga and Alvaro Carreras came in from Madrid’s 3-0 win at Valencia on November 7.

Real Madrid: Courtois, Alexander-Arnold, Huijsen, Konate, Carreras, Bernardo Silva, Camavinga, Arda Guler, Bellingham, Diomande, Mbappe

Substitutes: Andrii Lunin, Eder Militao, Vinicius Junior, Federico Valverde, Endrick, Aurelien Tchouameni, Marc Cucurella, Carlos Espi, Brahim Diaz, Antonio Rudiger, Denzel Dumfries, Thiago Pitarch

articles.title: Alonso highlights Chelsea ‘fragility’ after Leeds defeat
articles.summary: It was a miserable afternoon for the Blues at Stamford Bridge.
articles.content:
Alonso highlights Chelsea ‘fragility’ after Leeds defeat

It was a miserable afternoon for the Blues at Stamford Bridge.

Last Update:

Chelsea manager Xabi Alonso has admitted his side are going through a “delicate moment” after they were thrashed 4-1 by Leeds in the Premier League.

The Blues took the lead courtesy of Emanuel Emegha but, from there, the visitors ran riot, with goals from Noah Okafor either side of a Dominic Calvert-Lewin penalty and a late Brenden Aaronson giving Leeds their first win at Stamford Bridge this century.

The result saw Leeds leapfrog Chelsea, who drop to eighth in the table, as pressure begins to mount on the Blues boss.

Alonso spoke candidly after the game, admitting his team were in a tough period, with their confidence severely lacking.

“We are disappointed, we are sad,” Alonso told BBC Sport. “It was tough today, with the game, with the defeat. I think we are on a fragile moment right now.”

Blues need to ‘find solutions’

Reflecting on the game itself, the Chelsea head coach said his side needed to “find solutions” but insisted it was still early in the campaign.

“We lost a little bit of the confidence in the way we were playing and after that we were not able to regain. It’s a delicate moment but we need to go through it together, work and find solutions because there is a long way to go.

“But today it is tough to deal with.

“We could have done more, I was expecting more. We didn’t regain the confidence to have a real go and we couldn’t push hard enough to score one goal. That would have been enough but we didn’t do it.

“It’s the confidence, it’s this fragility at the moment – everything is related.”

Next up for Chelsea is a trip to Nottingham Forest next Friday, before hosting Crystal Palace the following Wednesday.

articles.title: Maresca: Manchester City in ‘a tough moment’ after Fulham stalemate
articles.summary: Maresca's side have now gone four Premier League matches without a win.
articles.content:
Maresca: Manchester City in ‘a tough moment’ after Fulham stalemate

Maresca's side have now gone four Premier League matches without a win.

Last Update:

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca admitted that his side were in “a tough moment” following a 1-1 draw with Fulham that left them four Premier League games without a win.

Elliot Anderson netted a wonderful volley in the second half at the Etihad to rescue a point for Maresca’s men after they had fallen behind to a Rodrigo Muniz strike after a quarter of an hour.

The hosts failed to make significant ground on their title rivals and current league leaders Arsenal, who could extend the gap on City to eight points with victory over Newcastle.

And Maresca was candid at full time, acknowledging his team were going through a difficult period.

“It’s a tough moment in terms of results,” he told TNT Sports.

“In this moment, the only thing we can do is try to recover – we have another big game on Tuesday so we need to focus on that.”

Speaking about his team’s performance, which improved after the break following a lacklustre first-half, the City boss said: “In the second-half we were much better. It’s also part of it when you are building something.

“We had so many moments when we could have made a better choice but it’s important that we arrive there, we create chances and we hopefully soon we can score more goals.”

Clean sheet record a ‘problem’

Next up for City is the visit of Napoli in the Champions League on Tuesday. However, they go into the game having not kept a clean sheet in nine consecutive fixtures in all competitions.

It is an unfortunate statistic that Maresca described as a “problem”, adding: “We are conceding many goals, especially at the beginning of games.

“We need to find a way to keep a clean sheet to help us win games.”

articles.title: Harry Kane sidelined for a ‘few months’ after undergoing surgery on ankle ligament tear
articles.summary: The Ballon d'Or winner hobbled off after 20 minutes during Bayern's clash with Koln on Friday.
articles.content:
Harry Kane sidelined for a ‘few months’ after undergoing surgery on ankle ligament tear

The Ballon d'Or winner hobbled off after 20 minutes during Bayern's clash with Koln on Friday.

Last Update:

England captain Harry Kane is set for a “few months” on the sidelines after tearing a ligament in his left ankle while playing for Bayern Munich, the club has said.

The 33-year-old, who was last month crowned the world’s best footballer after winning the Ballon d’Or award and then became England’s most-capped male player, was forced off after 20 minutes in Bayern’s 1-1 draw with Koln on Friday.

The striker suffered the injury following a challenge from defender Joel Schmied early in the game. He tried to continue but eventually had to be replaced.

In an update on Saturday, Bayern said that Kane had undergone “successful surgery overnight” on Friday and “will now begin his rehab”.

In the match, Bayern fell behind to a goal from England Under-21 player Mikey Moore – on loan at Koln from Kane’s former club, Tottenham.

However, the hosts were level 25 minutes later courtesy of Nathaniel Brown in what was Bayern boss Vincent Kompany’s first game back after a five-game absence.

Kompany was diagnosed with meningeal irritation – an inflammation of the protective membrane surrounding the brain and spinal cord – after collapsing at the club’s training ground last month.

Bad news for Tuchel

Kane’s injury came on the same day the Three Lions were drawn against Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals – repeat of last summer’s World Cup last-eight clash.

Kane had been instrumental in helping England finish top of their Nations League group, scoring in recent wins against Croatia and Spain earlier this month.

The two legs against Norway will be played on 27 and 30 March.

Following a prolific campaign last season, Kane has stared this one in similar fashion, netting four goals and registering eight assists in 10 league appearances this season,

He has also scored four goals and picked up three assists in four Champions League games.

The German champions are currently top of the Bundesliga and are unbeaten in all competitions so far this term.

However, Enzo Maresca’s men have the chance to make ground on the north Londoners – for a few hours at least – when they host Fulham in the early kick-off.

The Cottagers are languishing in 15th but have picked up two wins and two draws in their last four games – all without scoring more than a single goal in each.

For Mikel Arteta’s side, meanwhile, an arguably more daunting task awaits them. A trip to the north east to face a Newcastle team whose results so far this term have been patchy to say the least.

articles.title: Manchester United CEO says summer spending has made squad better and believes board are ‘laying the foundations’ for success
articles.summary: Omar Berrada is confident Manchester United are on the right track despite the club sitting in the Premier League relegation zone and with fans angry at issues off the pitch
articles.content:
Manchester United CEO says summer spending has made squad better and believes board are ‘laying the foundations’ for success

Omar Berrada is confident Manchester United are on the right track despite the club sitting in the Premier League relegation zone and with fans angry at issues off the pitch

Last Update:

Omar Berrada insists the Manchester United board are laying the foundations for the club to move forward and also defended their summer recruitment, insisting it has made the squad “fundamentally better”.

United’s off-field issues have been well documented with main shareholders the Glazers conspicuous by their absence while co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe has done little to improve performances on the field or relations with fans off it.

But club chief executive Berrada is confident the situation will improve with Mauricio Pochettino taking charge for the first time at Liverpool on Sunday.

In a wide-ranging interview with Sky Sports, he said: “I know it’s difficult to say this when you’re sitting 18th in the Premier League table. It’s clear – it’s not good enough, not acceptable, and that’s why we’ve made the change that we’ve made, so that we can move forward.

“But we are laying the foundations for sustained growth to put us in a position where we can be competitive consistently.

“The foundations are there. I am convinced that we are heading in the right direction. This is about doing everything we can to make our fans happy, and that means improving the results on the pitch, and that means getting a team that is performing to its maximum potential, that the fans can feel proud of.”

Some of the criticism from United fans has crossed the line – Berrada

United fans vented their anger at the last home game, with Aston Villa, chanting against the owners and hurling tennis balls on to the pitch.

Berrada admitted the criticism hurt but accepted it comes with the territory.

“It is our responsibility to run the club,” he added. “And, yes, coaches have a very important role to play. Players, of course, have to perform at the highest level consistently for any coach.

“They’re part of a club that when you’re wearing the shirt, you have an enormous amount of responsibility. And that responsibility means that you have to be giving your best every day in training, in the matches. And that’s the same for executives.

“Being in this position comes naturally with the criticism and the scrutiny that we’re going to get. We accept it, some of it is fair, some of it does cross the line.

“I think we do live in this world of social media, where people like to generate negative stories about the club because it drives more engagement, and it drives more general noise and activity around the club. But we park that.”

United spent around £163million in the summer with nearly all of it going on midfielders Carlos Baleba, Andrey Santos and Youri Tielemans.

That left the squad short of depth at left-back and in attack, but Berrarda insists they got their priorities right.

“You have to take it in the context of the last few years,” he said. “The summer of 2025, I think the recruitment team was widely praised with the four players that were signed. And they did very well. They helped the team achieve Champions League qualification.

“When we look at this summer, we went in knowing what we needed to do. Of course, there have been different dynamics at play. It’s probably been the summer or the transfer window where there’s been the highest inflation in transfer fees.

“And we’ve said publicly and we’ve said consistently in the last few years that we need to stay disciplined. We need to take the right decisions. We need to buy the right players for the right value at the right time in terms of what the squad needs.

“And when we look at the summer transfer window of 2026, I know we’re receiving a lot of criticism for it, but we’re actually happy with the players that we bought.

“We think that Carlos Baleba, Youri Tielemans, Andrey Santos, and Karl Darlow – and let’s not forget that we’ve also welcomed back Marcus Rashford, who had a very good season on loan at Barcelona – these are five additions that we think have made the squad fundamentally better.

“It’s true that we lost Casemiro, who is a top player and gave a lot to the club. We also lost Manuel Ugarte to, unfortunately, an ACL injury. So our focus was very much about straightening the midfield.

“When we started the transfer window, we really only had Kobbie Mainoo as our midfielder. So we wanted to reinforce that, and we did it.”

Pochettino has brought ‘passion and energy’ to Manchester United

Berrada concedes it was a difficult decision to sack Michael Carrick but has been impressed with the early days of Pochettino’s reign.

“He has a tremendous amount of passion and energy,” Berrada said of the Argentine. “We see it already in the two days he’s been with us.

“There’s a buzz about the place, and he’s brought that with his staff. He has a very clear philosophy, identity of how he wants to see the team play. And I think he’s coming just at the right time for him and us to be able to help the team and take us forward.

“He’s equally as ambitious as we are, which is: we want to win titles.

“You have to think that when you’re playing for Manchester United, when the results aren’t going well, the pressure and the scrutiny is enormous. And all that noise around the club and around the players can be difficult to manage.

“So I think in Mauricio we bring somebody that has just the right amount of maturity and experience at the big clubs to be able to put his arms around the players and to let them perform at their highest potential.”

articles.title: Premier League Predictions: Arsenal march on, Chelsea frustrated and Poch starts with a point at Liverpool
articles.summary: Club football makes a welcome return this weekend after the international break. There are some mouthwatering games to look forward to, so here are our Premier League predictions...
articles.content:
Premier League Predictions: Arsenal march on, Chelsea frustrated and Poch starts with a point at Liverpool

Club football makes a welcome return this weekend after the international break. There are some mouthwatering games to look forward to, so here are our Premier League predictions...

Last Update:

The final international fixtures of 2026 have been played and club football has a clear run into next year.

We are now 10 games in – the traditional cut-off point for assessments to be made and for chairmen to make managerial changes. Michael Carrick and Pierre Sage have departed with Mauricio Pochettino and Thomas Frank making their returns to the Premier League.

Pochettino has a baptism of fire this weekend when he takes his Manchester United side to Liverpool while Manchester City and Arsenal bookend Saturday’s action.

Here are the fixtures in full and our Premier League predictions.

SATURDAY

Manchester City v Fulham (12.30pm)It must have felt like a long international break for City boss Enzo Maresca following successive league defeats to Aston Villa, Brighton and Nottingham Forest. Maresca’s men are now third, six points behind leaders Arsenal. City have not lost four leagues on the bounce since 2024. Fulham are also mired in a poor run of form with their EFL Cup exit to Crystal Palace followed by successive draws with Aston Villa and Newcastle. Something has to give at the Etihad and it seems more than likely it will result in a City win.Prediction: Manchester City 3-0 Fulham

Aston Villa v Sunderland (3pm)Both these teams went into the break with an element of frustration. Villa’s previous game saw them squander a 4-2 lead at Manchester United to draw 4-4 after conceding two injury-time goals while Sunderland would have wanted to maintain the momentum gained from beating Chelsea at the Stadium of Light. The Wearsiders still sit in the relegation zone and their chances may hinge on the fitness of key men Granit Xhaka and Brian Brobbey, both of whom withdrew from international duty.Prediction: Aston Villa 2-0 Sunderland

Bournemouth v Nottingham Forest (3pm)Bournemouth have won their last eight in all competitions, storming up the table after a slow start. Nottingham Forest will be hoping for a similar resurgence, sparked by their 3-1 defeat of City before the international break. Eli Junior Kroupi’s return to fitness adds another element to the Bournemouth attack and it is hard to look past them in this one.Prediction: Bournemouth 3-1 Nottingham Forest

Chelsea v Leeds (3pm)Leeds’ record at Chelsea is rotten: the Yorkshire club have not won at Stamford Bridge since 1999 and were hammered 6-3 in West London in the EFL Cup earlier in the season. Daniel Farke’s side will travel south with a degree of confidence, though, following the 1-0 win over Spurs. Chelsea remain a model of inconsistency. Xabi Alonso’s men were beaten at Sunderland last time out and need to find a good run of form if they are to challenge for a top-four spot.Prediction: Chelsea 2-2 Leeds

Coventry v Crystal Palace (3pm)Thomas Frank takes charge of Crystal Palace for the first time and is immediately thrust into a relegation six-pointer at the CBS Arena. Palace have not won in the league for over a month and another defeat here would move the Sky Blues five points clear of the Eagles. Coventry have bounced back nicely after a slow start and their form at home will likely be key to remaining in the top flight. Prediction: Coventry 2-1 Crystal Palace

Tottenham v Ipswich (3pm)Was Tottenham’s three-game winning streak a genuine indication that this season will bring an improvement? Or was the limp second-half showing at Leeds a portent of what lies ahead? Saturday’s game with Ipswich could go some way to answering that question. The clash with the Tractor Boys is a game Spurs ought to be winning given their vast summer spending and it will be fascinating to see whether Roberto De Zerbi can get a tune out of his players. Ipswich have slipped to 14th due to a four-game winless streak and would love to replicate the 2-1 victory achieved on their last visit in 2024.Prediction: Tottenham 2-1 Ipswich

Newcastle v Arsenal (5.30pm)Arsenal continue to march on and five successive league wins have helped them establish a five-point lead at the top of the table. Three of their last four victories have come via a 1-0 scoreline in another example of Mikel Arteta’s preference for solidity over flair. In his defence, it is a strategy that worked last season and is almost certain to work again. Newcastle have failed to score in their last two home league games, against Everton and Aston Villa, and beating David Raya will be a tough task.Prediction: Newcastle 0-2 Arsenal

SUNDAY

Hull v Brighton (2pm)In theory, this is an away banker. The side most out of form in the Premier League against a team that has won six of their last seven in the top flight to climb to second. Hull’s limitations have been on show for some time with their last victory coming back in August. Brighton are trending in the opposite direction and Fabian Hurzeler’s men will head to East Yorkshire in confident mood, looking to keep the pressure on leaders Arsenal. Prediction: Hull 0-2 Brighton

Liverpool v Manchester United (4.30pm)Mauricio Pochettino’s first game as Manchester United boss would be a big occasion irrespective of the opposition but there is added spice given it comes against arch rivals Liverpool. The Argentine has an almighty job on his hands to turn the tanker round and get United moving in the right direction. A trip to Anfield would not have been his preferred game first up but they’re the cards he has been dealt. If he needs any encouragement it will come from the fact this is not a Liverpool side firing on all cylinders with Andoni Iraola’s methods still not fully engrained. United have not lost at Anfield since 2023 and won both league encounters last season.Prediction: Liverpool 1-1 Manchester United

MONDAY

Brentford v Everton (8pm)Brentford’s bright start has faded and one win in five league games means Keith Andrews’ side start the weekend in eighth place. The Bees remain strong at the Gtech Community Stadium, though, with just one defeat on home soil since February. Everton have won their last three in all competitions and David Moyes’ side have the physical strength and solidity to challenge any team in the league on their day. Jack Grealish’s return will add some spark to the Toffees’ attack.Prediction: Brentford 1-2 Everton
