articles.title: Pochettino impressed by ‘amazing’ commitment of Manchester United’s players ahead of Liverpool clash
articles.summary: Manchester United head to Liverpool on Sunday for Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge
articles.content:
Pochettino impressed by ‘amazing’ commitment of Manchester United’s players ahead of Liverpool clash

Manchester United head to Liverpool on Sunday for Mauricio Pochettino's first game in charge

Last Update:

Mauricio Pochettino says his first few days at Manchester United have provided optimism that the players, led by Bruno Fernandes, can turn their season around.

Pochettino was named the successor to Michael Carrick last week and flew into England on Wednesday to start work on a two-and-a-half-year contract.

He takes charge for the first time at Liverpool on Sunday as United look to move out of the Premier League relegation zone.

An expansively assembled squad has spectacularly failed to deliver this season with fans and media questioning their commitment but Pochettino believes he has seen enough already to expect an upturn in fortunes.

He said: ”Our job is to adapt and go ahead a little bit. The most important thing when you arrive at a new club is to understand the culture and identity. We already know what this club means to everyone. The players are the group of people who really care. They want to perform for fans, their friends and families. When we arrive, I feel they feel the responsibility. They are committed.”

Bruno is Manchester United captain – Pochettino

Captain Bruno Fernandes has come in for specific criticism with his form slipping well below the levels that saw him named the PFA Footballer of the Year last season. He was also dropped by Carrick for questioning the tactics in the 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como.

“I think the commitment of all the players is amazing from day one,” said Pochettino. “Bruno is our captain and he’s a very important player, but all the players must feel they are important. We chatted yesterday and spent three hours in my office with all the players. I missed some injured players, but in the next few days, I will talk to everyone.”

Pochettino traditionally employs a high-energy, high-press game that appears ill-suited to the United players at his disposal. Asked if the United players were fit enough, the Argentine said: “Good question. When we arrived, we found a group of players who we propose [the idea of] the football we feel. They buy that idea of being brave, but the thing is it’s a debate that I don’t like to go in because we cannot talk about things without context.

“We cannot talk about data without context. It is easy to manipulate data but it is true and we need to be honest sometimes they don’t show something that you can see on the field. We are here not to denounce things, but to build with the club.”

It’s on United coaching staff to restore confidence levels – Pochettino

United head to Anfield having claimed just eight points from their opening 10 games and Pochettino admitted it would take time to restore the players’ battered confidence.

“It’s normal, when you don’t win games, the confidence goes down,” he said. “I think the players need to feel something from us, which always happens when a new coaching staff comes in. I think the reception and the welcome in the last two days…today we were talking at the end of the training session, I said thank you because they made the effort. That is good.

“We need to settle our principles and apply our concepts. They have quality and we need to unlock things.

“We want to create something different and positive, to build our own way here. We feel the support from day one that we started to work. The most important thing is to think about the next action, not the past.”

articles.title: The drone footage was sent to me! Liverpool boss Iraola sees funny side of spying incident at Manchester United
articles.summary: Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola will have several key players back for Sunday's game with Manchester United, including captain Virgil van Dijk
articles.content:
The drone footage was sent to me! Liverpool boss Iraola sees funny side of spying incident at Manchester United

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola will have several key players back for Sunday's game with Manchester United, including captain Virgil van Dijk

Last Update:

Liverpool boss Andoni Iraola joked that the drone footage of Manchester United’s training session had been sent to him ahead of Sunday’s Premier League clash between the sides.

Pochettino’s work with the United squad on Thursday was captured and 12 minutes of it shared on YouTube with the operator since apologising and removing the video from the platform.

Iraola initially saw the funny side but then admitted it was a problem that could affect Liverpool in future.

“They were sending me the footage yesterday!” he said with a smile, before adding: “I think the important thing about this is that it shouldn’t be legal. It happened to Manchester United but it could happen to me in a training session in the future.

“The media had access to our training session yesterday for 15 or 20 minutes, so everyone knows who was training with us and who didn’t train. It isn’t about the advantage, it is the fact that there is a reason we train behind closed doors because there are some things that you have to respect. I don’t think it is nice for any club.”

Van Dijk fit to captain Liverpool against Manchester United

Liverpool head into the clash with their north-west rivals in fourth place in the Premier League table.

They will also be boosted by the availability of Virgil van Dijk, Jeremie Frimpong and Ryan Gravenberch.

“If everything goes to plan, they should all be available for the game,” said Iraola. “It is a matter of pain for Ryan Gravenberch, he is managing his situation a little bit but he has trained with us the past two days. Jeremie Frimpong is recovering in the same way, the international break helped with that. Virgil van Dijk is also fine to go.”

Conor Bradley and Giovanni Leoni are also back in training but won’t be considered for the weekend.

“It is very good news,” said Iraola. “The international break came at the best time for us because we got the chance to introduce them slowly into training with the rest of the players.

“They have already started doing things with the rest of the team in the latter part of this week. Obviously they are still not available but it is very good news that they are back doing things with the group.

“It is true that they will need to build up their training time slowly. Both of them are looking good though, so hopefully they can play in a few weeks’ time.”

It doesn’t get bigger than Liverpool versus Manchester United – Iraola

Iraola has yet to fully implement his style at Anfield and results have been inconsistent. But he is fully aware of the credit he will receive if Liverpool can see off a United side that will play under Pochettino for the first time.

He said: ”It is true that you don’t find bigger games than this. I feel lucky to be here and privileged to be part of this game.

“We have to acknowledge the importance of the game and all of its ingredients, such as their new manager, because that will be a challenge for us. It is important for us in lots of different ways because we want to improve our form at home and the first chance we have to do that is against Manchester United on Sunday.”

Pochettino only flew into England on Wednesday and has had little time to prepare for the game with his new players, but Iraola pointed out the bulk of his squad have also been away for the past fortnight on international duty.

“It’s true they have this disadvantage, [but it means] we don’t have the references like we do the other opposition,” he said. “The beginning of the game is important, we have to adapt to certain things. We know the players very well, strengths and weaknesses and until today that is not going to change from one day to the other.

“It’s natural every time there is a new manager, you want to impress. It happens everywhere but we are more focused on us and improving on our game. We haven’t had a lot of time with the players but we focus on us.”

Friday's Nations League draw has thrown up some fantastic ties

England will face Erling Haaland and Norway in the quarter-finals of the Nations League.

The draw was made on Friday morning and it pits Haaland against 2026 Ballon d’Or winner and England captain Harry Kane in a battle of arguably the two best number nines in world football. articles.title: There are no players here with privileges – Real Madrid boss Mourinho sends warning to Vinicius as suspension ends
articles.summary: Vinicius Junior is fit and available for Real Madrid this weekend but Jose Mourinho said there is no guarantee he just walks back into the side for the game with Celta Vigo
articles.content:
There are no players here with privileges – Real Madrid boss Mourinho sends warning to Vinicius as suspension ends

Vinicius Junior is fit and available for Real Madrid this weekend but Jose Mourinho said there is no guarantee he just walks back into the side for the game with Celta Vigo

Last Update:

Jose Mourinho is hoping Vinicius Junior returns from suspension ready to make a big impact at Real Madrid but stopped short of guaranteeing him an automatic place in the starting XI.

Vinicius has not played for Madrid in La Liga since October 10 after receiving a four-match ban following his red card against Villarreal with Yan Diomande sparkling in his absence on the left wing. It was another setback for a player who has struggled for top form recently and his admission this week that he did not work hard enough in pre-season raised eyebrows in the Spanish capital.

The 26-year-old Brazil international did his utmost to remind Mourinho of his ability with five goals over the international break, including a hat-trick in the 7-0 thrashing of Singapore on Tuesday.

Madrid face Celta Vigo at the Santiago Bernabeu on Saturday night and, when asked about Vinicius, Mourinho  said: “Starter, on the bench, in the stands… it doesn’t matter. It’s something strange because a couple of weeks ago Vini was the giant problem and after scoring with Brazil we’re now talking about whether he plays or not, if he has to play, I think it’s too much.

“What I say now I have already said, he is an incredible player, we love him and we need him, we help him but there are no players here with privileges. No-one has to play by decree.

“Madrid has to have a strong squad, with many good players, and that story of playing or not playing… there are 23 players or more who are going to force me to leave players in the stands and it is the life I want for Madrid. I don’t want 11 good players, I want many.”

Maybe Vinicius shouldn’t have made those comments – Real Madrid boss Mourinho

Asked to comment on Vinicius’ claims that he partied too much over the summer, Mourinho added: “It’s already over. Summer [is now] winter, hot and cold. The impact of the World Cup has passed, that stage for the boy has passed. He has done his self-analysis, maybe he could not have said it, but I never like to criticise the openness.

“Now we are going to get, I hope, to a situation in the league that will be decisive, and that is where Vini can make a difference, with the experience he already has, the player that everyone wants in the dressing room. Vini is one of them and is very determined to be decisive again in Madrid as he has been for many years.”

Another Brazilian, Endrick, has struggled for game time this season and admitted on international duty that he may have to consider his options in January if that situation does not change.

Mourinho is a fan of the 20-year-old but refused to offer any assurances and stressed the club’s needs will always take precedence.

He added: “For me Madrid is more important than Endrick. I love him very much and I have a lot of affection for him, I need him. [But] If Madrid decides a different thing, you have to respect that. That said, Madrid and I know he’s important.”

Madrid go into the weekend on the back of an eight-game winning streak in all competitions. They can join leaders Barcelona on 33 points with a victory against Celta. Barca host Villarreal on Sunday.

articles.title: Manchester United boss Pochettino boosted by return of key defensive duo for Liverpool clash
articles.summary: Manchester United have looked rudderless at times this season but they will have two experienced men at the heart of their defence when the Mauricio Pochettino reign gets underway at Liverpool on Sunday
articles.content:
Manchester United boss Pochettino boosted by return of key defensive duo for Liverpool clash

Manchester United have looked rudderless at times this season but they will have two experienced men at the heart of their defence when the Mauricio Pochettino reign gets underway at Liverpool on Sunday

Last Update:

New Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino is able to field an experienced central defensive pairing at Liverpool on Sunday with both Harry Maguire and Lisandro Martinez fit and available.

Maguire was taken off at half-time in United’s last game, a 4-4 draw with Aston Villa at Old Trafford, complaining of a back spasm.

But he took part in Pochettino’s first training session at Carrington on Thursday and is likely to be in the squad for the short trip down the East Lancs road at the weekend.

He could be joined in the starting XI by Lisandro Martinez, who has served his one-match ban for the red card he received at Chelsea on October 31.

Left wing-back Patrick Dorgu also took part in today’s session after missing Denmark’s games over the international break.

United predicament means there is no time for sleep – Pochettino

United head to Anfield sitting in 18th place in the Premier League table having won just one of their opening 10 Premier League games.

Pochettino was appointed last week as United boss, succeeding Michael Carrick, but only arrived in England on Wednesday after overseeing the United States’ Nations League win over Haiti in Cincinnati.

It has been a draining few days for the 54-year-old but he insisted now is not the time for sleep as he looks to inspire a group of players that have underperformed this season.

He told the club’s official website: “It’s a privilege to be, you know, head coach of Manchester United and I think we cannot waste time.

“We need to be ready to compete [on] Sunday. Now it’s not time to think about rest, it’s not time to think about sleep. It’s about being ready and to prepare everything to be sure that we are going to compete in the best condition at Anfield.”

Pochettino to live in the present with United in need of wins

Pochettino has made no secret of the fact the job at Old Trafford is one that has always appealed to him, especially as he came close to being appointed three times previously.

But he insists his focus is firmly on the present.

He added: “To be honest, dreams are dreams and are in a part of your heart and your brain. But I think I am a person that always… I live the moment, the present and try to be genuine, honest and loyal with your priorities and your present.

“And then, football will bring what football wants. But, of course, when [it] appeared, that possibility to be a head coach of Manchester United, you cannot turn [it] down and I know that it’s a massive responsibility but, at the same time, that responsibility is energy, it’s excitement, it’s about to give your best and to challenge yourself.

“I think it’s an amazing opportunity for us and that is why we are not wasting time. You know, another thing is to provide the best thing and the best platform for the football club to perform.”

articles.title: Veron compares Argentina star Nico Paz to Lionel Messi and Diego Maradona
articles.summary: Nico Paz has earned extraordinary words of praise from former Argentina international Juan Sebastian Veron, who has compared him to Lionel Messi and Diego Maradona
articles.content:
Veron compares Argentina star Nico Paz to Lionel Messi and Diego Maradona

Nico Paz has earned extraordinary words of praise from former Argentina international Juan Sebastian Veron, who has compared him to Lionel Messi and Diego Maradona

Last Update:

Former Argentina international Juan Sebastian Veron says Nico Paz is an “incredible talent” and sees shades of Lionel Messi and Diego Maradona in the 22-year-old Como star.

Paz is regarded as one of the brightest young talents in the game after a series of brilliant performances in Serie A and the Champions League while he enhanced his reputation further with two superb goals as Argentina beat Costa Rica 7-0 on Tuesday night.

Paz is now being talked about as the heir to Messi’s number 10 shirt and Veron can understand the fuss.

He told Gazzetta Dello Sport: “Nico Paz is an incredible talent. The future is his, if he continues to behave like a professional, as he is doing.

“At 22 years old, I have only seen Messi and a certain Diego Armando Maradona do things like he does. I don’t want to say that he will reach those levels, because that would mean becoming an absolute champion, a symbol of an era like Diego and Leo, each in their own way. But Nico Paz has the qualities to try. And I hope he succeeds.”

Paz gains Messi comparisons after brilliant spell with Como

Paz joined Como from Real Madrid in August 2024 and was named the best Under-23 player in Serie A after registering six goals and nine assists in his first season in Italy. He scored another 12 in 2025/26 to help Como qualify for the Champions League for the first time and, this year, has started superbly with six goals and eight assists in 14 games in all competitions.

Madrid reportedly have a buyback option which could be exercised if he maintains his current trajectory.

Asked what impresses him most about Paz’s game, Veron added: “Two things: the personality he shows on the field and the ease with which he executes certain plays. His personality is evident because his team-mates are looking for him, passing him the ball even when he is marked, knowing that he will dribble past his marker and escape. This means that everyone recognises his exceptional quality.

“Nico is a leader in the way he moves, in how he occupies space on the field, in how he directs the play, in how he decides when to accelerate or brake and, depending on how the play develops, choose to attack from the right, left or centre. He is at the centre of the game.”

Veron, who played for Boca Juniors, Lazio, Manchester United and Chelsea among others in his club career and is now president of Estudiantes, also sees comparisons to his own game, albeit in a different area of the pitch.

“You know that I don’t like to make comparisons with players from different eras, but I have to admit that Nico Paz is like Verón but 20 metres further up,” he said. “Free to look for the shot, the goal, the assist, the deep pass. He is a bonus for this Argentina team that tries to build in the post-Messi era.

“He is undoubtedly more of a forward than a midfielder, but he also has a great vision of the game and captures the rhythm of the game perfectly.”

Paz is more mature than Mastantuono – Veron

Veron believes Paz is further on in his development than Franco Mastantuono, who also scored twice for Argentina against the Costa Ricans.

Mastantuono, 19, is spending the season on loan at Fiorentina after struggling for game time at Madrid.

Veron said: ”He has extraordinary qualities, dribbles easily, is fast and has good execution speed. However, compared to Nico Paz, he is more immature, which is normal because he was born in 2007: he is three years younger. He certainly doesn’t lack class, technique or courage. In addition, if Real Madrid paid €45 million to River Plate to sign him, there must be a reason.

“If he will become a champion, I can’t guarantee it. However, I can say that Serie A is the most suitable league for a player like him. You have the opportunity to gain experience, to become familiar with rival defenders, to learn those technical and tactical tricks that the Italians master perfectly. However, he needs to find consistency in his performance, and this can only be achieved if he plays frequently as a starter, as is happening now at Fiorentina.”

articles.title: Manchester United’s current situation is a ‘mistake’ says Pochettino, who believes culture is key to improvement
articles.summary: New Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino is hoping to create a winning culture at Old Trafford ahead of his first match in charge, at Liverpool on Sunday
articles.content:
Manchester United’s current situation is a ‘mistake’ says Pochettino, who believes culture is key to improvement

New Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino is hoping to create a winning culture at Old Trafford ahead of his first match in charge, at Liverpool on Sunday

Last Update:

Mauricio Pochettino believes changing the culture at Manchester United is key to an improvement in performances.

The Argentine takes charge of United for the first time on Sunday when they head down the East Lancs road to Anfield to face arch rivals Liverpool.

Pochettino was appointed last week, succeeding Michael Carrick on a two-and-a-half-year contract, but only arrived in England yesterday after overseeing the United States’ Nations League win over Haiti in Cincinnati on Tuesday night.

He has had little time with his new players but has already outlined where he will focus his attention as he looks to guide United out of the relegation zone in the weeks ahead.

The 54-year-old told the club’s official website: “It’s a mistake to see the [current] situation. We need to see the potential of this club.

“Of course, the circumstances are the circumstances, and we need to be responsible for the circumstances. But at the same time, we need to understand that it’s a game and, to connect with the game, we need to feel free.

“The players need to express their talent. We need to create the environment and the platform for the players to perform. That is the most important thing and that is our priority now – it’s to work with them and try to take the pressure.

“Pressure needs to bring energy, responsibility needs to bring energy. Because if not, it’s too heavy to put all that pressure and responsibility on your back. When you connect with the game, you connect through your talent and when you feel freedom, when you feel happy, when you want to play for your team-mates, when you want to play for your family, when you want to play for your club, your fans.

“That is what we need to create all together and I think we have an amazing staff – we were talking a lot today. Then [we need to] settle all the principles and the ideas and to create our own philosophy and start from zero.

“I think with the power of this club and the fans supporting us, I think we will get in the place that we deserve to be.”

Creating a culture at United is key to success – Pochettino

He added: “To create the culture is the most important [thing]. Create the habits, the principles, and I think that is what we want to create.

“We need to [be] looking forward and to find a way to create the best habits and the culture that makes us close to winning every single game.”

United’s players have come in for heavy criticism this season, with fans directing their ire at the club’s predicament firmly in their direction.

But Pochettino says they will be supported behind the scenes to give them the confidence they need to thrive.

“The best squad that we can have are the players that we have and we need to love the players that we have. We need to support the players,” he said.

“We need to provide all the tools for them to perform. It’s only an act of responsibility now to start to work and provide them the facility to translate all their talent on the field.”

Ferguson is the best coach in the history of football – United boss Pochettino

Pochettino is the latest manager to try to replicate the achievements of Sir Alex Ferguson, who left Old Trafford in 2013 having won 13 Premier League titles and two Champions League crowns.

“For me, [he is] the best coach in the history of the sport,” Pochettino stated.

“I always admired him, and to have the possibility to meet when we went to Southampton and then we played in Old Trafford in 2013, yes, that dream came true. And then the possibility to meet him in a restaurant in London.

“Now being head coach is an hour and a privilege. That is the responsibility that brings full energy in my body, because the excitement to be here is massive.”

articles.title: I wouldn’t have done it for €20m – former Real Madrid star dismisses Ronaldinho stunt as a ‘complete farce’
articles.summary: Ronaldinho's return to professional football after 11 years has been condemned by former Real Madrid and Italy star Antonio Cassano
articles.content:
I wouldn’t have done it for €20m – former Real Madrid star dismisses Ronaldinho stunt as a ‘complete farce’

Ronaldinho's return to professional football after 11 years has been condemned by former Real Madrid and Italy star Antonio Cassano

Last Update:

Former Real Madrid forward Antonio Cassano has described Ronaldinho’s appearance for Ravenna as a “complete farce” and insisted he wouldn’t have done it for €20million.

Ex-Brazil and Barcelona playmaker Ronaldinho played 45 minutes against Forli in the Serie C clash last weekend, coming out retirement to make an appearance for a club in which he is a shareholder.

The 46-year-old, who is also a close friend of Ravenna president Ignazio Cipriani, failed to score his 300th professional goal but insisted afterwards he’d be tempted to play again.

Cassano, who made 39 appearances for Italy as well as enjoying spells with Roma, Madrid, AC Milan and Inter Milan among others, failed to see the point of the exercise and felt it was demeaning to a player of that magnitude.

He told After the Game: “I want to start by saying one thing, and that is that I have great respect for Ronaldinho, as a person and as a player. For me, he is still among the five greatest in history, along with Messi, Maradona, Ronaldo and, probably, Pele.

“But what he did the other day was very, very unpleasant to watch. At 46, in those conditions, what was he supposed to do? I didn’t understand it. He did it because he has a relationship with Cipriani, who is his friend. And because they gave him a lot of money.

“I don’t know. For me, it was a complete farce. I don’t know what other interpretation to give.”

Cassano surprised by Ronaldinho decision

Cassano is now 44 and has been retired for nine years. He says even a vast sum of money could not persuade him to pull on his boots and play professionally again.

He added: ”I would not have done it even if they had offered me €10 million. Not even €20m. I was surprised because he has always been humble and one of the greatest [players] in history. If they ask me to judge what happened, I would say it was a shame.”

articles.title: Pochettino gives first interview as Manchester United boss and says job is an ‘honour and a privilege’
articles.summary: Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino is excited by the challenge that awaits him at Old Trafford
articles.content:
Pochettino gives first interview as Manchester United boss and says job is an ‘honour and a privilege’

Manchester United boss Mauricio Pochettino is excited by the challenge that awaits him at Old Trafford

Last Update:

Mauricio Pochettino expressed his excitement at finally arriving at Manchester United today, describing his appointment at Old Trafford as an “honour and a privilege”.

Pochettino touched down in England this morning following a trans-Atlantic dash from the United States after overseeing the USA’s 2-0 win over Haiti last night.

His first United game comes on Sunday when they visit north-west rivals Liverpool.

Speaking to club channels at the Carrington training ground, Pochettino said: “Thank you so much, I’m very excited to be here. It’s an honour, it’s a privilege to be in this amazing club. I’m looking forward to starting work.”

United struggling in relegation zone

Pochettino has an awful lot to tackle with United mired in the Premier League relegation zone having won just one of their opening 10 games under his predecessor Michael Carrick.

He will be joined by his usual group of staff with a United statement adding: “Mauricio Pochettino has officially started work as Manchester United head coach, marking the start of a dream role for the Argentinian.

“Pochettino is joined at United by a team of loyal staff he has worked with at Espanyol, Southampton, Tottenham, Paris Saint-Germain, Chelsea and the USA. Join us in welcoming Jesus Perez, Miguel D’Agostino, Toni Jimenez, Alec Scott and Sebastiano Pochettino.”

Pochettino pens farewell message before heading to United

Pochettino has made no secret of the fact he found it difficult to leave his previous role with the United States, breaking down in tears at a press conference last week.

And he left another emotional message before boarding the flight to England, even referencing the song ‘Country Roads’ which was the team’s soundtrack throughout his tenure.

He wrote on Instagram: “It is never easy to say goodbye, especially after everything we experienced together. I always wanted the opportunity to coach in the USA, and I was very happy to have this chance with the national team. Two incredible years, with so many great moments and experiences that will stay with me always.

“From the challenges we faced at the Gold Cup to the excitement of the USA hosting the World Cup, and now finishing our time by reaching the semi-finals of the Nations League, I am proud of what we achieved.”

He added: “When we arrived, I wanted us to believe that we could compete with anyone. I hope today that belief is stronger, not only with the players but with everyone who supports this team. Not everything in football can be measured by results, and I believe we have helped build something important for the future of soccer in this country.

“This experience has re-energised me and given me so much, both in football and personally. I have discovered a wonderful country, made new friends and enjoyed so many of the traditions. Every time I hear Country Roads, I will forever think of all of you with a smile.

“Thank you to the players, staff, everyone at [the US national team] and all the supporters. Especially to those who believed in us and gave us this opportunity.

“Leaving is tough at this moment, but sometimes in football an opportunity comes that is impossible to say no to. I have always believed in following my heart, even when it means leaving a place where I have been very happy.

“I hope this team continues to grow and achieves all the success it deserves. Thank you USA.”

articles.title: Chelsea star Martinez backs Paz to inherit Messi’s number 10 shirt for Argentina
articles.summary: Argentina playmaker Nico Paz has been backed to take on the famous number 10 shirt worn by the likes of Diego Maradona and Lionel Messi
articles.content:
Chelsea star Martinez backs Paz to inherit Messi’s number 10 shirt for Argentina

Argentina playmaker Nico Paz has been backed to take on the famous number 10 shirt worn by the likes of Diego Maradona and Lionel Messi

Last Update:

Argentina goalkeeper Emiliano Martinez says Nico Paz has the quality to inherit the number 10 shirt from Lionel Messi.

Messi’s international retirement has left the shirt vacant after being worn by the eight-time Ballon d’Or winner for the majority of the 21 years he represented his country.

The shirt weighs heavy with Messi arguably the greatest player of all time and an icon in his homeland after leading Argentina to two Copas America and the 2022 World Cup crown. It has also been worn by Mario Kempes and Diego Maradona before Messi.

But Martinez, who last night set the record for the most clean sheets by an Argentina goalkeeper with 47 in the 7-0 hammering of Costa Rica, says Como star Paz could be the man to assume the mantle.

“I see him becoming more and more integrated into the group,” said Chelsea stopper Martínez. “Obviously, he needs that Argentine fighting spirit, and we’re helping him adapt. Honestly, he deserves this opportunity; he deserves to be here playing. The goals he’s scoring are a bonus.”

Paz already feels like a leader for Argentina – Martinez

Paz, who was born in Tenerife but declared for Argentina due to his father, scored twice in the win over Costa Rica and was again the star man before being taken off at half-time by boss Lionel Scaloni.

Martinez added: “If he maintains this humility, this current form, Nico Paz can clearly wear the number 10 for Argentina and shoulder that responsibility. We need players like him, who feel like leaders. He can lead us to win many matches.

“We have to help him. We are a national team. There are no egos here. There is hard work, humility, and respect.”

No Argentina player wore the number 10 shirt against Costa Rica with Paz wearing number 18.

The 22-year-old already has the nickname ‘The Heir’ in reference to his position as the man most likely to take on Messi’s role with Argentina following a brilliant start to the season with Como that has seen him score six times and register eight assists in 14 matches in all competitions.

There is, therefore, an element of pressure on his young shoulders and Paz himself is eager to focus on enjoying his football rather than get dragged down by expectation.

Asked about inheriting the number 10 shirt, he said: “The truth is that I don’t think about it. What I think about is enjoying days like today, having fun on the field because what I love most is playing football and on top of that representing the national team and representing so many people. I play for that and I want to keep doing it.”

articles.title: Pochettino arrives in England but what are his priorities as he attempts to end Manchester United tragicomedy?
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino has issues: a poor squad; a mutinous dressing room and people above him with dubious levels of football knowledge. How does he get Manchester United back on an even keel?
articles.content:
Pochettino arrives in England but what are his priorities as he attempts to end Manchester United tragicomedy?

Mauricio Pochettino has issues: a poor squad; a mutinous dressing room and people above him with dubious levels of football knowledge. How does he get Manchester United back on an even keel?

Last Update:

Mauricio Pochettino arrived at Manchester United’s Carrington training ground for the first time on Wednesday after flying in from the United States on a private jet.

His trans-Atlantic dash following the States’ 2-0 win over Haiti last night meant he reached Manchester four days before the weekend clash with arch-rivals Liverpool at Anfield.

It is a difficult opening game for Pochettino, who now has to wait to discover whether his international players will arrive back with a clean bill of health.

Pochettino has signed a two-and-a-half-year deal at Old Trafford and is tasked with transforming a club that has grown used to mediocrity. United go into the weekend in 18th place in the Premier League, inside the relegation zone and only one point above rock-bottom Crystal Palace.

The 54-year-old is already talking in bullish tones, telling former City winger DaMarcus Beasley of his intention to make United the strongest club in Manchester.

Here are five things he needs to do to make that happen:

STOP THE BLEEDING

Before any thoughts of trying to take on Manchester City, Pochettino needs to ensure United aren’t dragged into a season-long relegation battle. Michael Carrick’s side won just one of their opening 10 games, with five draws and four defeats. Granted, a trip to Anfield is tricky but what comes after, in the Premier League at least, ought to give reason for optimism. Brentford at home, Newcastle away, Coventry at home and Crystal Palace away is a dream set of fixtures to get points on the board. And with the season still in its relative infancy, two or three victories would soon propel United up the table.

CREAKING DEFENCE PROVIDES LITTLE STABILITY

The old adage about good teams being built from the back still rings true, just take a look at Arsenal. United have shipped 19 goals in their 10 Premier League games this season with only Ipswich and Coventry conceding more. Cynics will point to a dreadful summer recruitment programme that targeted midfielders at the expense of other positions, leaving Carrick short of options at the back. They have been ruthlessly exposed. Of the regular starters, Diogo Dalot seems to be suffering from being the butt of the fans’ anger, Harry Maguire looks a shadow of the player he once was while Ayden Heaven and Leny Yoro continue to look short of confidence and the physicality required. Pochettino is regarded for his attacking philosophy but that is no good unless there is a strong base to work from. January reinforcements are a must.

LACK OF DYNAMISM IN MIDFIELD

Another issue that can be tracked back to the summer and the woeful recruitment overseen by director of football Jason Wilcox. In Kobbie Mainoo, United possess one of the most talented young midfielders in England but his apparent weakness is a lack of mobility. So what did Wilcox do? Sign Youri Tielemans and Andrey Santos at a combined cost of £85million. Two players that are neat on the ball but lack mobility. Carlos Baleba also arrived and, while he can get round the pitch, he spends most of his time getting round the treatment table. United need athleticism in midfield, otherwise they will get overrun. Pochettino needs to be knocking on Wilcox’s door.

FERNANDES LINGERS AS DO ISSUES

Bruno Fernandes remains arguably United’s best player but his presence continues to divide. The Portuguese has not hit the same level as last season, when he was rightly named PFA Player of the Year. And his criticism of Carrick’s tactics following the Champions League pasting at Como undoubtedly weakened his manager’s position. Fernandes has a reputation for playing for himself despite wearing the captain’s armband and, while that might not be entirely fair, his fingerprints always seem to be all over the club’s various crises. Reports suggest he has turned down a new contract, although United do have the option to trigger a 12-month extension next summer. The prudent way forward would be for United to extend his deal and then look for a buyer. Fernandes turns 33 next year and a fresh start may benefit all parties.

IMPLEMENT A STYLE OF PLAY – IN TIME

One of the biggest criticisms of Carrick was his teams didn’t have a discernible style of play. It seemed jumbled, one day playing with swagger, the next in a low block. Some would argue that showed tactical flexibility but what was the default? Pochettino has always employed a high-energy, high-press gameplan that has proved to be hugely effective. Given the inadequacies of the United squad, will he able to do that from the off? Most likely not and fans understand that. But it has to happen over time (one of football’s most precious commodities). United lack an identity and Pochettino has to change that.

articles.summary: Turkey midfielder Arda Guler has signed a new deal at Real Madrid, the club confirmed this morning
articles.content:
Real Madrid confirm new contract for Arda Guler, who wants to ‘follow in the footsteps of legends’

Turkey midfielder Arda Guler has signed a new deal at Real Madrid, the club confirmed this morning

Last Update:

Real Madrid have announced Arda Güler has signed a new contract that ties him to the Spanish club until 2032.

The 21-year-old has been one of Madrid’s better players this season and this deal demonstrates his growing importance to Jose Mourinho’s side.

A Madrid statement read: “Real Madrid CF and Arda Güler have agreed to extend our player’s contract, and he is now linked to the club until June 30, 2032.

“Arda Güler arrived at Real Madrid in July 2023, at the age of 18. In his four seasons defending our shirt, he has played 126 games, and has won five titles: one Champions League, one Club World Cup, one European Super Cup, one La Liga and one Spanish Super Cup.

“He is a Turkey international, a team with which he has played 38 games so far.

“Last September he received the Breakthrough Player Award for the Champions League 2025-2026.”

Real Madrid boss Mourinho key to Guler development

Mourinho’s arrival at the Santiago Bernabeu has helped solidify Guler’s role within the team and the Portuguese has been richly rewarded with the former Fenerbahce man contributing four goals and six assists in 14 games in all competitions this season.

Mourinho has played him predominantly in a more attacking role rather than a central midfielder.

That has provided Guler with a clearer path into the starting XI, given the competition for central midfield places from players including Jude Bellingham, Bernardo Silva, Federico Valverde, Eduardo Camavinga and Aurelien Tchouameni.

Madrid were initially forced to be patient with Guler as he adapted to the demands of playing for one of the world’s biggest clubs.

His situation is now very different, with the club viewing him as an increasingly important part of their first-team plans.

Guler – I want to follow in the footsteps of Real Madrid legends

Guler had a message for the Madrid fans after penning his new deal.

He said: “History you made, history to be made.

“When I first put on the Real Madrid shirt, I knew that I was going to be part of an immense history. Today I feel the same pride and happiness, but with an even greater responsibility.

“Following in the footsteps of legends who have written their names in football history, in the biggest club in the world, is a great honor for me. My dream is to wear this shirt for many years, win new titles together, and someday leave my own mark on this unique story.

“I want to thank everyone who has always been by my side since my first day: especially our president, Florentino Perez, my family, my colleagues and all the staff and coaches I have worked with. And the most special thanks, to Madrid fans all over the world, who have always given us endless support. Here’s to many more beautiful days together!

“Very happy to continue to be a part of this club. 2032.”

articles.title: Argentina boss Scaloni hails brilliant Paz but says even Messi couldn’t do it without a supporting cast
articles.summary: Nico Paz starred once again as Argentina thrashed Costa Rica 7-0 in a friendly in Cordoba
articles.content:
Argentina boss Scaloni hails brilliant Paz but says even Messi couldn’t do it without a supporting cast

Nico Paz starred once again as Argentina thrashed Costa Rica 7-0 in a friendly in Cordoba

Last Update:

Argentina boss Lionel Scaloni was impressed by Nico Paz in the 7-0 demolition of Costa Rica but warned the Como playmaker can’t carry a team on his own – a point even the great Lionel Messi recognised.

Paz enhanced his burgeoning reputation with two goals as Argentina cruised to a routine win in Cordoba – their first success since Messi retired from international football.

The 39-year-old leaves an enormous gap to fill but fans have already labelled Paz ‘The Heir’ and he did little to quell their enthusiasm with another superb display.

Paz, who was born in Spain but has an Argentine father, scored twice as did Julian Alvarez and Franco Mastantuono, adding to a goal from Alexis Mac Allister.

Scaloni said: “He is not going to solve the game alone; he has moments like today and what he does is help the team. And that’s the important thing: first the team and then the individual. If the best player in history [Messi] understood it and needed his team-mates to win, how can the youngest not need them?

“He is a player who can give even more. Today he played a very good game, like the other day. We’ll take care of him. We are very happy with him.”

Scaloni proud of Argentina’s 2026

The win brought the curtain down on Argentina’s 2026 campaign, highlighted by their run to the World Cup final.

Scaloni added in remarks reported by Nacion: ”I am satisfied for having done a good job and having always tried to be competitors, winning or not. The national team always tries to have an identity and that’s what fills us with pride.

“We have competed, we have reached the World Cup final, we have shown our face in all the matches. But you don’t always win.

“We try to make the fans happy watching the national team play. The feeling is that when the national team plays everyone gets together. We have not been able to bring them the World Cup, which is what hurts us the most, but we have generated a feeling that even if we do not win, the work can be recognised.”

Scaloni was delighted with the crowd at the Mario Kempes Stadium after the defeat to Uruguay last week was played at a half-full Bombonera in Buenos Aires.

“[We got a] Wonderful reception from the people,” said Scaloni. “I’m amazed with Cordoba. People stayed to the end. They have not lost their love for the national team.

“It is clear that we have to continue competing so that it stays this way.”

articles.title: Wayne Rooney reveals he contemplated suicide at Manchester United as he opens up on ‘lowest point’ of his life
articles.summary: Wayne Rooney reveals he contemplated suicide during his Manchester United career and credits wife Coleen with helping him through his darkest period.
articles.content:
Wayne Rooney reveals he contemplated suicide at Manchester United as he opens up on ‘lowest point’ of his life

Wayne Rooney reveals he contemplated suicide during his Manchester United career and credits wife Coleen with helping him through his darkest period.

Last Update:

Wayne Rooney has revealed he contemplated taking his own life during the height of his Manchester United career, opening up about the mental health struggles he experienced despite his success on the pitch.

The former England captain admitted he would isolate himself at home and spend days drinking, even after getting married and welcoming his first child, Kai.

Speaking on the Life At The Midpoint with Gabby Logan podcast, Rooney explained how his struggles left him unable to enjoy what should have been one of the happiest periods of his life.

“I can look back and say I was selfish, but I knew I was going through something which I was really struggling to deal with,” he said.

“Then I didn’t want Kai seeing me like that, so that’s why I’d hide away as well.

“I got to a place where you’re contemplating suicide. You just didn’t want to be around anyone. I didn’t want to be see people in the streets. I didn’t want to go into shops.

“I was always comfortable on a football pitch, but everything else [I] really struggled with it.”

Rooney explained that he found it difficult to acknowledge his struggles because he feared appearing weak, despite seeking professional help.

“You don’t want to show any weakness, so you try to mask it,” he continued.

“Even though I knew the position I was in, it was difficult to actually admit that I was in that in that position because I felt like you feel less of a man if you like for doing that.”

Rooney credits wife Coleen with helping him through difficult period

The former United striker revealed that he began speaking to a therapist in an attempt to understand why he was struggling.

“I was speaking to a therapist to try and figure out what was up with me because when I look back I was probably at the height of my career, I’ve just had a young son, I’ve just been married,” Rooney explained.

“It should be the happiest point in my life and it wasn’t.

“It was probably the lowest point because of the selfish acts I was taking.”

Rooney, who is currently appearing on ITV’s I’m A Celebrity… Get Me Out Of Here!, also credited his wife Coleen with providing vital support during that period.

“Coleen helped me massively. She could have walked away, it was that bad, but she stuck by me and helped me get through it,” he said.

articles.title: Get Gibbs-White and dump Fernandes! Former Manchester United winger says Forest midfielder should be primary target for Pochettino
articles.summary: Ashley Young reckons Morgan Gibbs-White is a perfect fit for Manchester United
articles.content:
Get Gibbs-White and dump Fernandes! Former Manchester United winger says Forest midfielder should be primary target for Pochettino

Ashley Young reckons Morgan Gibbs-White is a perfect fit for Manchester United

Last Update:

Former Manchester United winger Ashley Young says Mauricio Pochettino should look to sign Morgan Gibbs-White as the long-term successor to Bruno Fernandes.

Young, who won the Premier League, EFL Cup and Europa League during an eight-and-a-half-year spell at Old Trafford, believes Fernandes is past his peak and thinks Nottingham Forest midfielder Gibbs-White is the man to replace him.

In the latest episode of the Overlap Daily, in conjunction with Sky Vegas, Young said: “Fernandes has been unbelievable for the club. The standout performer. But there’s been so much that’s come about…has he turned down another contract? You want to build around a player. He’s 33 next year.

“Now, for me, and I’m going to throw a name out now…I would go and sign Morgan Gibbs-White.  A number 10, you want to build a team around a player.”

Eyebrows were raised when Forest spent £42million on signing Gibbs-White from Wolves in 2022 but he has proved a shrewd acquisition. He came close to joining Tottenham in 2025 but, instead, signed a new, three-year deal at the City Ground.

The 26-year-old has won 10 England caps and is widely considered one of the best attacking midfielders in the Premier League.

And Young believes he is now ready to join a club of United’s stature. He added: “I think that he’s young, he’s hungry, he’s just got into an England squad. I think he’s got the capabilities to go and play for – no disrespect to Nottingham Forest – a bigger club.

“I think he’s shown more than enough at Nottingham Forest to be able to go and say, do you know what, I could play for a bigger club like Manchester United and take the weight of that. For Morgan Gibbs-White, he’s now around the England squad. Players talk. Players will talk, and you’re looking at other players around the England squad and you like [the idea of] playing for the title.”

Young says Pochettino needs time to succeed at United

United head to Liverpool on Sunday afternoon mired in the relegation zone but with Mauricio Pochettino in charge for the first time following his appointment last week.

Young says the Argentine needs time to mould a squad that is able to play his high-intensity brand of football.

He said: “They’re going to need to raise money, aren’t they? They’ve got to get rid of players. And I’m sure that’s what Pochettino is going to be saying. If you look at his Tottenham sides, he rebuilt them. They were, I think, 16th at the time [when he arrived]. They finished fifth in his first season, [and reached the] League Cup final.

“After that, they were top four, Champions League football. It takes time, and I’m sure he would have said to the board, ‘I’m going to need time, because you can’t just give me a January window and a summer transfer window and expect results to change’. Because it won’t happen.”

articles.title: Former Arsenal hero questions Saka impact and says Dowman is the man to spark life into Gunners’ attack
articles.summary: Arsenal winger Bukayo Saka has not kicked on the way Charlie Nicholas expected and the Scot wants to see Max Dowman given more of a chance
articles.content:
Former Arsenal hero questions Saka impact and says Dowman is the man to spark life into Gunners’ attack

Arsenal winger Bukayo Saka has not kicked on the way Charlie Nicholas expected and the Scot wants to see Max Dowman given more of a chance

Last Update:

Former Arsenal striker Charlie Nicholas says the Gunners are “not getting enough from” Bukayo Saka and suggested Max Dowman be given more of a chance to bring some sparkle to their attacking play.

Saka has endured a stop-start season so far with a quad injury sustained against Bayern Munich seeing him miss the last five Arsenal games, as well as England’s Nations League wins over Croatia and Spain.

The 25-year-old is not expected back this weekend when the leaders head to Newcastle.

Saka burst on to the scene in the 2019/20 season with 26 league appearances and has gone on to become a mainstay for club and country on the right wing, culminating in a major role as Arsenal clinched the Premier League title in May.

Despite that, Nicholas, who played for Arsenal during the 1980s, thinks the Londoner’s progress has stalled.

He told Footy Accumulators: “Watching Arsenal at the moment, things are going really well. However, Bukayo Saka is a great talent, but I just feel there’s something more that I need from him.

“I just don’t think England and Arsenal are getting enough from him. His goalscoring and assists are pretty good, but it’s not kicked on in the way that two years ago I thought it would. He’s had a couple of injuries here and there, but I think he could do more and reach higher.

“I watch players like Lamine Yamal, and I think with Saka there’s too many square passes, whereas two years ago he was more likely to take players on inside and out.

“Maybe he needs a break to focus his attention. I see it on the sideline with Mikel Arteta – he’s constantly on top of Saka. He seems to ask more out of him, and it’s as if he still needs to find a little bit more.”

Nicholas not convinced by Arsenal’s attacking output

Arsenal are five points clear at the top of the Premier League table despite not hitting top gear, especially in attack. Arteta’s side have scored 15 goals in their 10 games, 11 fewer than second-placed Brighton.

Nicholas added: “I have to be honest, I believe Arsenal will win the title this season, but I was expecting a little bit more extravagance from them. It’s still not properly filtering through yet; each game is still this hard-working structure and shape off the ball. I’ll applaud it as long as they keep winning, but I’d like them to be a little bit more entertaining.”

Former Scotland international Nicholas believes Dowman, who yesterday became the youngest-ever goalscorer for England Under-21s in their 3-2 win over France aged just 16 years and 320 days, could inject some much-needed dynamism into Arsenal’s attack.

“I’d like to see Max Dowman more,” said Nicholas. “When I was young and put in the team, I was fearless and tried to do things.

“I know he got sent off the other week [against Fleetwood in the EFL Cup], but watching his balance and the natural way he moves makes me want to get off my seat. Arteta should be giving him 20 minutes each game instead of five at the end.

“I just think that would excite everybody again, as well as giving a challenge to the likes of Saka.”

Dowman has made just two Premier League appearances for Arsenal this season, with both coming off the bench.

articles.title: Hat-trick hero Vinicius Jr plays down angry gesture after substitution and backs Brazil boss Ancelotti’s decision to rotate
articles.summary: Vinicius Jr grabbed a hat-trick as Brazil thrashed Singapore 7-0 in an international friendly on Tuesday
articles.content:
Hat-trick hero Vinicius Jr plays down angry gesture after substitution and backs Brazil boss Ancelotti’s decision to rotate

Vinicius Jr grabbed a hat-trick as Brazil thrashed Singapore 7-0 in an international friendly on Tuesday

Last Update:

Vinicius Junior dismissed suggestions he had fallen out with the Brazil staff following his earlier-than-expected substitution against Singapore and said his focus now was on returning to Real Madrid in top condition.

The 26-year-old completed a confidence-boosting few days with a hat-trick as Brazil thrashed the Asian minnows 7-0 on Tuesday, building on his brace in the weekend defeat to Japan.

The Madrid winger, who played as a number nine, netted a 12-minute hat-trick in the first half to put Brazil in control. It was a welcome return to form for Vinicius who has struggled in the early weeks of the season.

“My first time [scoring a hat-trick for Brazil], I hope it will be the first of many,” he said in remarks reported by AS. “We came into the game full of concentration. We knew the opponents were of a much lower level, but we still had to make the game easy.

“I think we managed to play well, create good opportunities. I could have scored some more, but I’m leaving happy for the game, for the victory and now it’s time to go back to our clubs, prepare well, because we have to go back 100%.”

Brazil forward Vinicius – I wanted to play longer

Endrick, Willian Estevao and Rayan were also on target for Brazil with Raoul Suhaimi’s own goal completing the rout. It was a timely win for boss Carlo Ancelotti, who watched from the stand following his red card against Japan.

Vinicius was taken off just shy of the hour mark and appeared to gesture angrily to the bench, seemingly unhappy with his withdrawal.

But the former Flamengo man insisted it was not a big deal.

He added: “The plan was for me to play 15 or 20 more minutes and I always want to score more goals.

“I understood that it was necessary for other people to play, and Allan had to participate. This period is for preparation, for testing, and the coach did it, he got everyone to play. Now we have to define the squad because the [Copa América] qualifiers are approaching.”

Baby joy for Brazil star Endrick

Endrick dedicated his goal to his new-born baby.

The Madrid forward said: “My wife gave birth. He is a wonderful child, and my wife is also very happy. The goal was for him, for my wife, who is a very strong woman.

“I know it’s not easy. I came to represent Brazil, which is one of the most wonderful things in the world. And she was one of the first to encourage me to come and represent my national team. She’s at home taking care of him.”

articles.summary: Tuesday's Tip of the Day predicts disappointment for both Northern Ireland and Wales
articles.content:
Tip of the Day: Northern Ireland and Wales to find going tough in Nations League

Tuesday's Tip of the Day predicts disappointment for both Northern Ireland and Wales

Last Update:

Tuesday’s Tip of the Day focuses on the Nations League and the final matches before attention turns back to  domestic matters.

Like it or loathe it, the Nations League does create narratives and there are two tonight that feature home nations.

The first will determine whether Northern Ireland will secure promotion to League A and a chance to mix it with the big boys. Michael O’Neill has done a remarkable job with the Ulstermen and they head to Hungary knowing a draw will see them secure top spot in Group B2.

The problem is they will come up against a side that has arguably more quality, led by Liverpool duo Dominik Szoboszlai and Milos Kerkez.

Szoboszlai has been passed fit and will captain his country in Budapest. A Hungary win would see them leapfrog the Irish and we just can’t see past the hosts.

Wales are also in action tonight when they come up against a Portugal side without the now-retired Cristiano Ronaldo and smarting from a 4-1 hammering by Denmark at the weekend.

Craig Bellamy’s side will definitely finish last in Group A4 and enter the promotion/relegation play-offs, while the Portuguese require a point to ensure they finish first.

Jorge Jesus will name a strong side with the likes of Bruno Fernandes, Vitinha and Joao Neves all set to start.

articles.title: Mowbray steps back from role at Blackburn due to health issues
articles.summary: Tony Mowbray has stood down from his role as Blackburn boss due to health issues
articles.content:
Mowbray steps back from role at Blackburn due to health issues

Tony Mowbray has stood down from his role as Blackburn boss due to health issues

Last Update:

Tony Mowbray has stepped back from his role as Blackburn boss due to health issues.

Mowbray returned to Ewood Park over the summer after being forced to leave his position at Birmingham having been diagnosed with bowel cancer in February 2024.

After surgery and chemotherapy he decided to make a comeback and had been performing a typically impressive job with Blackburn 13th in the Championship table.

But a statement from 62-year-old Mowbray, who has also managed Middlesbrough, Sunderland and West Brom among others, today read: “Unfortunately, due to health issues, I have to step back from my role as head coach of Blackburn Rovers.

“I’m immensely proud of this group of players. Their dedication and professionalism have given us some memorable performances and wins, and I’ve loved working with them.

“Thank you to my coaching staff for all your hard work and for the support you’ve given me. It’s been a pleasure working alongside you.

“To the fans, thank you for the way you’ve supported me and the team this season. I’ve always tried to give you a team that you can be proud of. Your support has meant a great deal to me.

“I’m grateful to the owners and COO Suhail Shaikh for giving me the opportunity to lead this great club once again.

“I’d ask that you give me and my family privacy at this time. Thank you for your understanding.”

We’re very fond of Tony – Blackburn owner Rao

Rovers’ owner Mr B Balaji Rao added: “Our thoughts are with Tony and his family as he steps back from his duties to focus on his health.

“Through our many meetings over the years, we’ve come to know Tony well and grown very fond of him. We’ve always admired his professionalism, his dedication and the passion he brings to his work at Blackburn Rovers.

“Tony, please know that you have our unconditional and unwavering support. We send you and your family our love and strength, and we will do all we can to support you through this time.”

articles.title: Van Hecke ‘ashamed’ as Netherlands ‘fold like a pack of cards’ on memorable night  for Wirtz and Germany
articles.summary: It was a sobering night for the Netherlands in Berlin and defender Jan Paul van Hecke says the players need to do much better
articles.content:
Van Hecke ‘ashamed’ as Netherlands ‘fold like a pack of cards’ on memorable night  for Wirtz and Germany

It was a sobering night for the Netherlands in Berlin and defender Jan Paul van Hecke says the players need to do much better

Last Update:

Netherlands defender Jan Paul van Hecke says the players “should be ashamed” of their performance following the 5-0 hammering by Germany.

The Tottenham centre-half pulled no punches after a woeful Dutch display in Berlin with Jurgen Klopp’s Germany leapfrogging Orange and Greece to finish top of Nations League Group A2.

Florian Wirtz scored twice for the hosts as the Netherlands suffered their first defeat under Xavi, just three days after they thrashed Greece 7-0.

Van Hecke told NOS: “The worst thing is that you normally have a base to fall back on, but it wasn’t there at all today. Then you see the result that follows.

“Everything went wrong. We should be ashamed. Everything folded like a pack of cards. And me too, it starts with myself. Everyone has to look in the mirror and sort themselves out, because it’s just not good enough. It is inexplicable.

“We can say all kinds of things, but everyone can see that this is not good enough, that it is ridiculous.”

Things have to change – Netherlands defender Van Hecke

Despite the defeat, the Dutch still qualified for the quarter-finals but they will encounter a strong last eight that includes Germany, France, Belgium, England, Spain and Portugal. The final qualifier will be determined tonight.

“Things definitely have to change, because this is just not possible,” said Van Hecke. “You play for the Dutch national team and you play Germany, then this kind of thing can’t happen, right? I think a lot of other boys and girls would have wanted to be on the pitch.”

Xavi apologised to the Dutch supporters for the limp display against their biggest rivals.

He said: “I talked to the players to understand what happened. First of all, we must apologise to the supporters. We didn’t play football and didn’t show spirit. As a coach, I don’t understand that.

“We played an historic match against Greece, with intensity and passion. Today was the opposite. Maybe it’s because I’m new and need to understand the players. Maybe it’s a lack of mentality too.

“It’s bitter. I’m disappointed and sad, because until today I was very proud of the players. But today was a shock for me as a coach. It is what it is, but we cannot accept it. We need to change a lot of things from today. It was embarrassing.”

It was fun for us – Germany star Wirtz

It was a dark night for the Netherlands but one that signals Germany are on the right track under Klopp.

His side topped the pool courtesy of a better head-to-head record than the Netherlands and Greece, with all three sides finishing on 11 points.

Wirtz was the star man with a scintillating display. “We hope that we can make it fun for the fans. It was definitely fun for us, especially in the second half,” the Liverpool playmaker told German broadcaster ARD.

“We don’t mind who we play. We want to play attacking football. We want to score goals and dominate the opponent – and I think we did that perfectly.

“We want to keep going next year. We want to get better. I think we’ve taken some great steps in our development as a team.”

articles.title: Portugal boss Jesus addresses Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother: ‘No way around it’
articles.summary: Cristiano Ronaldo retired after being left out by Portugal
articles.content:
Portugal boss Jesus addresses Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother: ‘No way around it’

Cristiano Ronaldo retired after being left out by Portugal

Last Update:

Portugal head coach Jorge Jesus has praised Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother, Dolores Aveiro, after the 71-year-old claimed the striker had been “deceived” by the Selecao before retiring from international football earlier this month.

In a lengthy statement after leaving Portugal’s Nations League camp in September, the all-time top scorer for his country claimed new boss Jesus had “broken his word” to him, leading to the Portuguese Football Federation suspending and fining their greatest icon of modern times.

On Sunday, Aveiro said she joined Ronaldo in feeling “sad” about the situation and described herself (via ESPN) as “glad” about Portugal’s “well-deserved” 4-1 home defeat to Denmark on Saturday in their first game since his retirement.

“Now I have to respond to Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother?” Jesus asked on Monday, speaking to RTP and SportTV, via Abola.

“My mother, too… Cristiano Ronaldo’s mother is a lady I greatly respect. What can she say? A mother is a mother. There’s no way around it. I understand her statements.”

Cristiano Ronaldo: What did Jesus say about Aveiro?

Jesus, who led Ronaldo’s club side, Al-Nassr, to the Saudi Pro League title last season, said Aveiro would naturally back the 41-year-old.

Aveiro is said to have worked long hours as a cook and cleaner to support her four children when they were growing up as part of a modest background in Funchal.

Describing herself as “proud of my family above all else”, Aveiro has more than five million followers on Instagram and regularly uses the platform to post about the five-time Ballon d’Or winner.

Portugal paid tribute to the absent Ronaldo before the game against Denmark but Aveiro said their displays “should be held in his presence”.

“Our tribute will take place here at Sporting CP,” she suggested, speaking at the club where Ronaldo began his career.

“They value him here. [In the national team] he wasn’t respected – not even by his own teammates.”

“Noise?” asked Jesus. “It’s true, but a mother is a mother. I just have to respect her. A mother always defends her children, even to death.

“She is a very dear mother who suffered a lot to raise her children.”

Ruben Neves: Portugal ‘grateful’ to Cristiano Ronaldo

Ruben Neves called the atmosphere in Portugal’s camp “fantastic” but said the players “would like things to calm down” regarding Ronaldo.

“Whenever a player comes to a press conference, whenever a player comes to an interview, we are questioned about it – which is perfectly normal, given that it’s a player of Cristiano Ronaldo’s stature,” added the midfielder.

“When will this end? Maybe when the questions about this end and when the interviews about this end. Cristiano himself put an end to it and made a statement when his participation with the national team ended.

“We are immensely grateful to Cristiano; we are extremely grateful for everything he did for the national team and for Portuguese football but, from the moment he finished, we have to be the ones to stand up… in victories and defeats.”

What’s next for Portugal without Ronaldo?

Having suffered their first defeat since Jesus’ appointment in July, Portugal need a draw to guarantee winning their Nations League group when they visit Wales, who are bottom, on Tuesday (19:45 GMT).

“We weren’t the best in the world when we won four games in the last training camp and we’re not the worst because we lost this game,” reflected Neves.

“We are all professionals and very experienced and we know that now we have to stand up for the national team. The noise doesn’t affect our performance on the pitch at all.

“We certainly hope that things will calm down and that these questions will become less and less frequent so that we can focus on what is really important now, which are the games.”

Portugal are certain to reach the quarter-finals of the competition, which take place over two-legged ties in March. The draw to decide their opponents will take place on Friday (11:00).

articles.title: Argentina boss Scaloni makes Lionel Messi retirement prediction, drops coaching hint
articles.summary: Lionel Messi helped Argentina reach the 2026 World Cup final
articles.content:
Argentina boss Scaloni makes Lionel Messi retirement prediction, drops coaching hint

Lionel Messi helped Argentina reach the 2026 World Cup final

Last Update:

Argentina head coach Lionel Scaloni has predicted that Lionel Messi will play for at least four more years and claimed the icon could soon join his coaching staff.

Albiceleste record scorer Messi retired from international football on August 31 but remains a prolific captain for MLS team Inter Miami.

“I think he’s going to continue playing beyond 2030,” said Scaloni, who was briefly an international teammate of Messi and won the 2022 World Cup and 2021 and 2024 Copa America titles as his manager.

“He’s already said no to playing for the national team but, as a footballer, I hope he continues as long as he can.”

Lionel Messi: ‘No problem’ to become Argentina coach

Walter Samuel, who was also one of Messi’s Argentina teammates between 2005 and 2010, has been Scaloni’s assistant since his appointment in 2018 but announced last week that he will leave the role at the end of the year.

Former centre-back Samuel wants to become a manager and Scaloni laughingly suggested Messi could replace the 48-year-old.

“If he wants to come here, there’s no problem now that Walter’s not here,” Scaloni said, via Ole.

Lionel Messi contract, salary

Messi remains the most high-profile player in the world alongside Cristiano Ronaldo and joined Miami in July 2023 on a deal until 2025.

Now 39, he signed a new contract at the club in October 2025. Earlier this year, co-owner Jorge Mas said Messi’s salary is between $70 million (around £53m) and $80m (£61m) when all elements of his deal are included.

Mas explained that the scale of Messi’s contract makes it essential for the club to maximise sponsorship opportunities and commercial partnerships.

“The reason that I need to have sponsors and for them to be world-class is because players are expensive,” Mas told Bloomberg, adding that the money is “worth every penny”.

Lionel Messi stats

Formed by a group including former England captain David Beckham in 2018, Miami made Messi one of the most high-profile MLS signings of all time and won their first trophy with his help by triumphing in the 2023 Leagues Cup.

They lifted the Supporters’ Shield the following year, the MLS Cup in 2025 and the Campeones Cup in 2026.

Eight-time Ballon d’Or winner Messi was named the MLS Most Valuable Player in 2024 and 2025 and won the Golden Boot in the division in 2025 and 2026.

articles.summary: More teams have discovered their Nations League fates
articles.content:
Nations League results today: Greece edged out as Slovenia enter play offs

More teams have discovered their Nations League fates

Last Update:

Greece narrowly missed out on the Nations League quarter-finals as Matchday 6 of the 2026/27 campaign continued on Monday.

Ivan Jovanovic’s side beat Serbia at home but Germany and the Netherlands pipped them to the last eight after Die Mannschaft thrashed Oranje 5-0 in Berlin.

Slovenia beat North Macedonia and will enter the play-offs for promotion to League A, although they would have finished second in their group regardless of their result because Scotland, who will stay in Group B, lost in Switzerland.

Iceland also won promotion to League B by beating Luxembourg and the Faroe Islands won a League C decider for a play-off berth by seeing off Moldova.

Greece vs Serbia: Masouras goal not enough for hosts

Giorgos Masouras struck from close range during the second half as dominant Greece finished their first League A campaign by winning 1-0 against Serbia, who finished without a point.

The result means Greece will remain in the top flight and receive a favourable seeding in the draw for EURO 2028 qualifying on December 6, while Serbia will enter the play-offs, which take place alongside the quarter-finals at the end of March. All ties are two-legged.

North Macedonia vs Slovenia: Play offs beckon for runners-up

Danijel Sturm scored twice and David Zec also netted as Slovenia finished behind Switzerland but four points above third-placed Scotland in their group.

They now enter the play-offs to rise to League A, while North Macedonia finished without a point and will attempt to avoid relegation to League C.

Full Nations League results: November 16 2026

In League C, Aki Samuelsen’s first-half winner proved the only goal of the game as the Faroe Islands reached the play-offs to win promotion from League C and ensured Moldova will stay in the third tier.

Slovakia, who had already won the group and promotion, stayed unbeaten courtesy of a 95th-minute equaliser in a 2-2 draw at fourth-placed Kazakhstan.

Estonia won 2-1 at home to third-placed Bulgaria but must enter the play-offs because Iceland’s 3-0 home win over Luxembourg meant they won their group and direct promotion to League B.

Gibraltar earned a late draw with Malta and Lithuania won at home to Liechtenstein in Group D, from which all teams will be promoted.

articles.summary: Thomas Frank has returned to the Premier League after being appointed as the new boss at Crystal Palace
articles.content:
BREAKING: Crystal Palace confirm appointment of Thomas Frank

Thomas Frank has returned to the Premier League after being appointed as the new boss at Crystal Palace

Last Update:

Thomas Frank has been named the new manager of Crystal Palace on a two-and-half-year contract.

The Dane succeeds Pierre Sage, who was sacked last week with the club bottom of the Premier League, table having taken seven points from their opening 10 matches.

Frank has been out of work since being dismissed by Tottenham in February but will be in the Eagles’ dugout when they head to Coventry for a crunch relegation battle on Saturday.

Frank flopped at Spurs but made his name during an impressive spell at Brentford, during which he helped establish the Bees as one of the most progressive clubs in the Premier League.

A post shared by Crystal Palace Football Club (@cpfc)

Frank says managing Palace is ‘an honour’

Frank told Palace’s official website: “It’s an honour to sit here and be in charge of this fantastic football club. I’m really, really looking forward to it.

“Crystal Palace is an iconic club in England and in the Premier League. I will do everything I possibly can to help and support the players and everyone around the place, and I’m really looking forward to meeting them.”

Palace chairman Steve Parish added: “I’m delighted to be able to welcome Thomas to Crystal Palace. He has a proven track record of both creating winning teams and improving players, making him the perfect fit for our club.

“I’m confident Thomas’ extensive experience in the Premier League will help us achieve our goals for the rest of the season.”
