articles.title: BREAKING: Manchester United confirm Michael Carrick has been sacked
articles.summary: Manchester United have confirmed the sacking of Michael Carrick
articles.content:
BREAKING: Manchester United confirm Michael Carrick has been sacked

Manchester United have confirmed the sacking of Michael Carrick

Last Update:

Michael Carrick has been sacked as Manchester United head coach, the club have confirmed.

The announcement was widely expected after United co-owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe met CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox in Monaco to discuss Carrick’s position on Wednesday.

United States boss Mauricio Pochettino is expected to take over at Old Trafford.

Carrick arrived at United’s Carrington training ground at around 8am this morning and left two-and-a-half hours later. Reports suggest he was given the news of his dismissal by Berrada.

A club statement read: “Manchester United can confirm that Michael Carrick has departed his role as men’s first-team head coach.

“Michael rejoined the club in January and guided the team to a third-placed Premier League finish by winning 12 out of the remaining 17 games of the 2025/26 season, accumulating the highest points tally in the league during that period.

“After a disappointing start to the season, the club has come to the extremely difficult conclusion that a change is necessary in order to achieve our ambitions.

“Michael is, and always will be, a Manchester United legend. Just as he did as a player, he has conducted himself with the highest standards of dedication and professionalism throughout his time back with the club. His leadership and achievements last season will always be fondly remembered.

“The club intends to appoint a permanent successor as quickly as possible.”

United ditch Carrick with club in relegation zone

Carrick took over on an interim basis in January, succeeding Ruben Amorim, and inspired a dramatic uptick in performances that resulted in a third-placed finish and qualification for the Champions League.

He was rewarded with a two-year deal but this season has not gone to plan. Many fans put it down to underwhelming recruitment in the summer with Wilcox bolstering the midfield with the likes of Youri Tielemans, Carlos Baleba and Andrey Santos but leaving the squad short in other areas, most notably left back and attack.

United sit in 17th place in the Premier League table having won just one of their opening 10 games. It is their worst start since the 1986/87 season.

The club have fared a little better in the Champions League with two wins, against Sabah and Roma, but also defeats to Atletico Madrid and Como.

Carrick has also had to deal with two of his senior players making unwanted public statements. The first saw Argentina defend Lisandro Martinez criticise the club hierarchy following the defeat at Atletico while captain Bruno Fernandes questioned Carrick’s tactics after the 4-1 thrashing in Como.

Pochettino the next man to try to revive ailing United

Pochettino signed a new, four-year deal with the United States Soccer Federation in August but has made it clear to United officials he wanted to move back to the Premier League, where he has managed previously with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.

He led the USA to the last 16 at the World Cup over the summer with an exciting, young dynamic team that was able to produce the aggressive, high press style that Pochettino likes to employ.

The former Argentina defender, who has also managed Espanyol and Paris Saint-Germain, may find that more difficult at Old Trafford with a team lacks dynamism.

It is expected United will trigger his release clause with US Soccer of around £7.4million and he will be in charge for United’s next league game, against Liverpool at Anfield following the international break.

His long-time assistant Jesus Perez will also join him at Old Trafford.

The US face Haiti in a two-legged CONCACAF Nations League quarter-final tie over the next week. It is not yet known whether Pochettino will remain in charge for those games.

articles.title: Say no Mauricio! The five reasons why Pochettino should swerve Manchester United job
articles.summary: Mauricio Pochettino should stay clear of Manchester United. Here's why...
articles.content:
Say no Mauricio! The five reasons why Pochettino should swerve Manchester United job

Mauricio Pochettino should stay clear of Manchester United. Here's why...

Last Update:

Michael Carrick was this morning sacked as Manchester United head coach with Mauricio Pochettino the club’s top target to replace him at Old Trafford.

United are set to trigger Pochettino’s £7.4million release clause with US Soccer and appoint him prior to the game with Liverpool following the international break.

Carrick’s departure will bring an end to a fortnight of speculation over his future, along with media briefings and meetings in Monaco while, the man himself, showed up dutifully at Carrington to take training and attempt to lead a mutinous squad.

Whatever his failings as a manager, Carrick deserved better than this grubby treatment from Omar Berrada, Jason Wilcox and Jim Ratcliffe.

So, on to the next man and his attempts to turn round the tanker. Step forward Pochettino, a man who has come close to the United job several times before.

But why on earth would he want to walk into this? Here are five reasons why he should stay clear.

WORKING FOR THE THREE STOOGES

The chaotic and undignified manner of Carrick’s departure is a neat encapsulation of the way Ratcliffe, Berrada and Wilcox have operated at United. The lack of class is unbefitting Manchester United and should send red flags to any incomer. The trio continue to make the wrong calls on a staggeringly regular basis, displaying a level of incompetence that makes you query how they ever reached this level of prominence. From backing Erik ten Hag, despite interviewing replacements, the appointment of Ruben Amorim, the decision to go with a caretaker manager in Carrick (when does that ever work long term?)… every single call has been wrong. And that’s even before you get to Ratcliffe’s overall tenure that has included the redundancies of hundreds of loyal club employees and the alienating of fans due to draconian ticketing policies.

SPECTRE OF GLAZERS LINGER OVER OLD TRAFFORD

Pochettino is a fine manager – his record proves that. But, no matter what happens on the pitch, United will never feel a happy football club until the Glazers sell up. And with no sign of that happening, there will always be a disconnect between fans and ownership. As the manager, and the man who has to face the media every week, Pochettino will be caught in the middle. At the first sign of trouble, the green and gold will reappear and the protests will start and he will be front and centre.

A SQUAD THAT HAS SEEN OFF ANOTHER MANAGER

You almost have to admire the longevity of a group of players that have achieved very little. Ten Hag came and went following fall-outs with the likes of Harry Maguire and Marcus Rashford. Amorim also tried to get rid of the England forward and reportedly had disagreements with Kobbie Mainoo. Carrick had a very public spat with captain Bruno Fernandes while Lisandro Martinez showed his contempt for the club by blasting the summer recruitment programme despite producing shocking individual performances on the pitch. Trying to get a dressing room of egos pulling in the same direction is not easy. You wouldn’t mind quite so much if they could back it up with results but these players have won one league game this season and sit inside the Premier League relegation zone.

A SQUAD THAT IS NOT EQUIPPED TO PLAY THE POCHETTINO WAY

Wind back to Pochettino’s exciting Tottenham team that reached the 2019 Champions League final and you think high energy and high press. Full-backs Kieran Trippier and Danny Rose bombing forward, Dele Alli and Son Heung-min pressing high up the field and a world-class centre forward in Harry Kane. Compare that to the squad he will inherit at United. Diogo Dalot and veteran Luke Shaw have neither the energy, nor the quality of Trippier and Rose, there is no way Fernandes will press the way Son did and United’s expensive number nine Benjamin Sesko is an extremely poor relation to Kane. Sesko also spends most of his time on the treatment table. This squad needs a huge overhaul (again) but Wilcox’s record in the transfer market suggests he is not the man to do it. Pochettino fell out with the Chelsea owners over a lack input on transfers. Don’t be surprised if that happens again.

WHY GIVE UP A GOOD THING?

Pochettino signed a new, four-year contract with the United States Soccer Federation in August that was intended to provide stability and allow him to mould a squad for the 2030 World Cup. He was already making strides with his energetic young side reaching the round of 16 at this summer’s event, staged in the US, Mexico and Canada. Since then, he has introduced the likes of 16-year-old Cavan Sullivan, 17-year-old Mathis Albert with both youngsters getting their first goals in impressive wins over Chile and Mexico. The future looks bright. In addition, Pochettino has a nice lifestyle. He can travel round the States largely unnoticed, and also has the time and freedom to return to Argentina whenever he wants. Compare that to the goldfish bowl of Manchester and the enormous pressure of coaching a club of United’s stature. There is also the chance his reputation will be damaged by the mere association with United. Since Alex Ferguson left in 2013, the club has hired numerous big-name coaches: Jose Mourinho, Louis van Gaal, David Moyes, etc and every single one left damaged, scarred by the experience.

articles.title: Former Real Madrid star Toni Kroos takes aim at Barcelona and claims they aren’t good enough defensively to win the Champions League
articles.summary: Toni Kroos believes Barcelona will be exposed defensively against the better teams in the Champions League
articles.content:
Former Real Madrid star Toni Kroos takes aim at Barcelona and claims they aren’t good enough defensively to win the Champions League

Toni Kroos believes Barcelona will be exposed defensively against the better teams in the Champions League

Last Update:

Former Real Madrid midfielder Toni Kroos says Barcelona are not strong enough defensively to win the Champions League.

Barca have won three of their four European games this season with the only defeat coming in a 4-2 reverse at two-time defending champions Paris Saint-Germain on October 20.

They also top La Liga having won 11 of their first 12 fixtures, amassing 48 goals and conceding just 13. They are three points clear of Madrid, although Jose Mourinho’s side did win the season’s first Clasico at Camp Nou.

Hansi Flick has had to mix and match at centre-half this season with the likes of Andreas Christensen, Gerard Martin and Eric Garcia all taking their turn alongside Pau Cubarsi.

Kroos believes that is a fundamental problem for Barca that will be exposed by the better sides as they look to win the Champions League for the first time since 2015.

The ex-Germany international said: “Barça always tries to generate more chances than its opponents, but in the Champions League you find teams capable of scoring several goals in the same game.

“You also face rivals who defend exceptionally well and don’t let you play as you usually do. In those situations you have to know how to defend yourself.”

Bayern Munich have better defensive options than Barcelona – Kroos

Kroos highlighted another of his former clubs, Bayern Munich, as a better bet to land European football’s biggest prize due to the pace and athleticism in their back four.

He added: ”Barcelona don’t have someone like [Bayern’s Dayot] Upamecano, a defender that you can leave completely alone in a one-on-one, with 30 metres of space behind, and have the peace of mind that he will solve the situation.

“With players like Upamecano or [Alphonso] Davies I wouldn’t worry about defending those 30 metres. But with [Joao] Cancelo, Gerard Martín and similar players, it’s much more complicated.”

Cubarsi is Barcelona’s best defender

Kroos, who won the Champions League five times with Madrid and once with Bayern, did reserve words of praise for Cubarsi, who at 19 years of age, is arguably the best young defender in world football.

“He is by far their best defender,” he said. “He has the strength to win individual duels and the speed to face complicated situations. But when I look at the other defenders, I don’t see anyone I would trust.”

Barca return to La Liga action a week on Sunday when Villarreal visit Camp Nou. Their next Champions League game is on November 25 when they visit Azerbaijani minnows Sabah.

England captain Kane backs Pochettino to shine at Manchester United

Harry Kane enjoyed his time at Tottenham under Mauricio Pochettino and has backed the Argentine to shine if he gets the Manchester United job

Last Update:

England captain Harry Kane has described Mauricio Pochettino as a “fantastic manager” as the Argentine closes in on the Manchester United job.

Pochettino has reportedly agreed terms on taking over at Old Trafford with Michael Carrick likely to be sacked at the conclusion of talks in Monaco today between the club’s minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe, CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox.

Kane was a key part of the Tottenham side that finished second in the Premier League in 2017 under Pochettino and then reached the Champions League final two years later.

And the Bayern Munich striker, who will win his record-breaking 126th cap for England against Croatia at Wembley on Thursday, had nothing but positive things to say about his former boss.

“Me and Mauricio have a fantastic relationship. I mentioned him as one of the managers who had a big impact on my career,” said Kane. “I needed his guidance. He pushed me on and off the pitch which was really helpful.

“He’s a fantastic coach, he’s managed the biggest clubs in the world. From my point of view I can’t speak highly enough of him. We’ll have to wait and see what happens but I know he’s a great guy but also a fantastic manager.”

My dream is to win a major trophy with England – Kane

Kane is currently riding the crest of a wave after winning the 2026 Ballon d’Or followingb another brilliant year with Bayern and England.

However, it has not always been this way with the 33-year-old facing the possibility of going his entire career without a major trophy before landing the Bundesliga title in his second season in Germany.

He was a key member of the England team beaten in successive European Championship finals, by Italy in 2021 and Spain in 2024.

“After any big loss, especially a final loss, emotions are very high,” he added. “I don’t think I ever doubted that it would come. It was frustrating not to have reached that yet in my career. A lot of these moments you have to get over quickly.

“In the last couple of seasons my game is at the highest level so that could be a factor of that.

“To win a team trophy with England, a major trophy, is my biggest dream. It’s always been my biggest dream to win a European Championship, a World Cup or both hopefully. I know how difficult that is so extremely motivated to do that. I’m surrounded by great teams both club and country so hopefully it is an exciting time ahead.”

Kane aware of free-scoring Lankshear

Kane is coming towards the end of his career, giving England a major headache with no obvious successor standing out.

Middlesbrough’s Will Lankshear has been mentioned as one to watch following his move from Spurs to Teesside over the summer and Kane said he is aware of the 21-year-old, who has scored 13 goals in 13 Championship games this season.

He said: ”I wouldn’t say I have followed his whole career but obviously this season it has been hard not to hear about him and he has done extremely well at Middlesbrough. I spoke to a friend who coached him here at Tottenham [where today’s news conference was held] at the younger age groups who said he is a goalscorer.

“He has that goalscoring instinct. He’s still early in his development. I think what he is doing right now is perfect for him, playing loads of games, scoring goals, getting confidence. Whether he comes into the senior [England] side is down to Thomas [Tuchel]. It’s not a time to put too much pressure on him.

“There’s a lot of talk about who is going to replace me when I’m not here anymore. Just let him do what he is doing and I think it is great for his development. He’s doing really well.

“As the time goes on, I’m sure he will be on the right path to get his chance. If he does make it into the senior team it would be great to work with him and try and help him develop as a player.”

articles.title: Thibaut Courtois: I loved Xabi Alonso but Real Madrid needed Jose Mourinho
articles.summary: Real Madrid needed a head coach with the authority of Jose Mourinho, according to goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois
articles.content:
Thibaut Courtois: I loved Xabi Alonso but Real Madrid needed Jose Mourinho

Real Madrid needed a head coach with the authority of Jose Mourinho, according to goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois

Last Update:

Real Madrid goalkeeper Thibaut Courtois remains a big fan of Xabi Alonso but admits the club needed someone with the presence of Jose Mourinho.

Alonso was brought in to much fanfare in 2025 after guiding Bayer Leverkusen to their maiden Bundesliga title and was expected to galvanise a Madrid squad that surrendered their La Liga crown to Barcelona, lost to their arch-rivals in the final of the Copa del Rey and crashed out of the Champions League to Arsenal in the quarter-finals.

But it did not pan out that way with Alonso departing after less than eight months in charge following reported disagreements with president Florentino Perez and star striker Kylian Mbappe.

Courtois was saddened by Alonso’s failure at the Santiago Bernabeu and is taking a keen interest in how he gets on at one of the Belgian’s former clubs, Chelsea.

He said: “When results go wrong, it’s always easy to point at the coach. In some cases the dynamic was not good, but with other players it was. I loved it. I liked the way he trained. He is a great coach and, if they give him time [at Chelsea], he will do well.”

Jose Mourinho ‘fills the room’ – Real Madrid star Courtois

Alonso was replaced by Alvaro Arbeloa at Madrid but the former Spain full-back struggled to win over a difficult dressing room that imploded with reports of widespread disagreements culminating in a training ground fracas between Aurelien Tchouameni and Federico Valverde that left the latter requiring hospital treatment.

Arbeloa left at the end of last season with Perez deciding a firm hand was needed. He opted for Mourinho who returned to the club 13 years after his first spell came to an acrimonious end.

And Courtois, who worked under the Portuguese during his time at Chelsea, feels it was a sensible appointment.

“I was very happy with his return, I was excited,” said the Belgium international. “He wrote to me when he arrived in Madrid, but I ignored his message for two weeks. I was on a flight and didn’t see it!

“He tells us that he has matured, that with experience he is calmer. At Chelsea he was harder in the dressing room, but he still has the same personality. He fills the room; you can see his presence when he enters the dressing room. We needed something like that.”

Bellingham key to Real Madrid revival

Mourinho’s impact was not instant but the results are now starting to arrive. Madrid went into the international break on the back of eight successive wins in all competitions, including a 2-1 victory at Barcelona that suggests this year’s title race is wide open.

Key to their success has been the form of Jude Bellingham. The England midfielder, who was this week named in the FIFPro World XI alongside team-mate Mbappe as well as Lionel Messi, has scored five goals and added two assists in 16 games and Courtois is full of praise for the former Borussia Dortmund man.

“I value Bellingham very much. He is a great person, a good friend and a great footballer,” said Courtois. “He had a great first season, but last year, like everyone else, didn’t play like he can. He also had a great World Cup; he was the best player for England. Now he is showing that level in Madrid and he is very important for us, both with the ball and in defensive tasks. I hope he ends up winning many titles.”

Madrid, who are second in the table, three points behind Barca, return to La Liga action a week on Saturday with a home game against Celta Vigo.

articles.title: Wayne Rooney confirmed as a contestant on I’m A Celebrity… Get Me Out of Here!
articles.summary: Wayne Rooney will head to the Australian jungle to compete in the ITV show this month
articles.content:
Wayne Rooney confirmed as a contestant on I’m A Celebrity… Get Me Out of Here!

Wayne Rooney will head to the Australian jungle to compete in the ITV show this month

Last Update:

Wayne Rooney has been confirmed as one of the stars heading into the jungle for the next series of I’m A Celebrity… Get Me Out of Here!

The former England striker, who remains Manchester United’s all-time record goalscorer with 253 in a 13-year career at Old Trafford, joins the likes of Kaiser Chiefs frontman Ricky Wilson, Paralympian and presenter Ade Adepitan, actress Claire Sweeney and broadcaster Mariella Frostrup in the ITV show.

Rooney’s wife Colleen took part in the programme in 2024, coming second to Danny Jones. The first episode of this, the 26th series, is aired on Monday, November 16.

“If you’re going in you want to win it,” Rooney said. “Coleen’s already tried and obviously she finished second in the show so I’m here to bring that title back to the Rooney household.”

The Liverpudlian does not sound an ideal candidate to cope with life in the wilds of Australia with the programme traditionally starting with the contestants jumping out of a plane. It also contains challenges that sees contenders have to eat various grubs and parts of a Kangaroo’s anatomy.

Rooney added: “I’ve been booked to jump out of a plane three times before and never made it on the plane. I don’t like snakes or what is in the water either – I don’t go in the sea.”

Rooney retired from playing in 2021 having been appointed the permanent manager of Derby. The 41-year-old had subsequent managerial spells at DC United in Major League Soccer, Birmingham and Plymouth.

He is also a pundit on the BBC’s Match of the Day.

articles.title: Van Dijk will play on next season even if Liverpool don’t extend his contract
articles.summary: Virgil van Dijk is not panicking despite the fact he is out of contract at Liverpool at the end of the season
articles.content:
Van Dijk will play on next season even if Liverpool don’t extend his contract

Virgil van Dijk is not panicking despite the fact he is out of contract at Liverpool at the end of the season

Last Update:

Virgil van Dijk says he won’t retire at the end of the season, even if he is not offered a new contract by Liverpool.

The 35-year-old’s current deal at Anfield expires in June 2027 and talks are expected to start in the coming weeks over a renewal.

Van Dijk has played every minute for the Reds this season and has shown little sign of regression despite his age, forming a strong central defensive pairing with new signing Jeremy Jacquet.

And the Netherlands international is eager to continue playing whatever happens at Liverpool.

Speaking after the win at Crystal Palace on Sunday, he said: “I want to keep playing and continue what I’m doing so let’s see what the season brings.

“I’ve had an amazing time already so far. If that will be extended, that’s the case. If not, then I will go somewhere else. There’s nothing to report at the moment but that doesn’t mean that there’s any stress or anything.

“I feel good but it’s not about me at the moment. I’m not in any panic whatsoever.”

Liverpool defender Van Dijk struggling with a ‘little niggle’

Van Dijk has been forced to withdraw from the Netherlands squad for the games with Greece and Germany due to injury but he was quick to stress it was nothing serious.

He added: “Mentally I’m in a good place, physically I’ve been struggling with a little niggle the last couple of weeks but I do everything in my power to be out there.”

It would be a surprise if Liverpool opted against giving Van Dijk at least one more year, especially as the club are short in defence following Ibrahima Konate’s move to Real Madrid.

Jacquet is thriving but Joe Gomez’s fitness continues to be a concern, and his contract is also up next summer, while Giovanni Leoni is sidelined after tearing his ACL.

articles.summary: James Hill has been rewarded for his fine form for Bournemouth with a call-up to the England squad
articles.content:
Hill called up to England squad as cover for Konsa

James Hill has been rewarded for his fine form for Bournemouth with a call-up to the England squad

Last Update:

Bournemouth defender James Hill has been called into the England squad.

Hill gets his chance after Ezri Konsa was ruled out for Thursday’s Nations League game against Croatia. The Arsenal defender is set to return for Sunday’s clash with world champions Spain, however.

Hill, 24, has made 15 appearances for Bournemouth this season and has been one of their star performers in a superb run that has seen Marco Rose’s side win their last seven games in all competitions.

An FA statement this morning read: “AFC Bournemouth defender James Hill has received his first call up to the England squad.

“The 24-year-old, who represented his nation at MU20 and MU21 level, has joined the Three Lions ahead of the forthcoming Nations League fixtures.

“Meanwhile, Ezri Konsa will not be in contention for Croatia at Wembley on Thursday as he continues to follow his own programme but will return to full training later this week before Sunday’s trip to Spain.”

Bristol-born Hill joined Bournemouth from Fleetwood for a fee reported to be in the region of £1million in 2022. He had loan spells at Hearts and Blackburn before nailing down a regular spot in the Cherries’ back four last season.

Dan Burn was also called up yesterday following Marc Guehi’s withdrawal.

articles.title: Real Madrid’s forgotten man Endrick hints at January move despite Mourinho support
articles.summary: Endrick could push for a move away from Real Madrid in January after seeing his opportunities restricted this season
articles.content:
Real Madrid’s forgotten man Endrick hints at January move despite Mourinho support

Endrick could push for a move away from Real Madrid in January after seeing his opportunities restricted this season

Last Update:

Real Madrid’s forgotten man Endrick is determined to repay Jose Mourinho for his backing but has not ruled out leaving the Santiago Bernabeu in January.

The Brazil international has joined up with his national team ahead of international friendlies against Japan and Singapore and will be hoping to get some game time after a frustrating spell in the Spanish capital.

An injury sustained in August saw him miss four weeks and he has struggled to make an impact since then. He has started just one game this season, the victory over Sevilla, and has managed a combined 140 minutes of action in all competitions.

Endrick spent the second half of last season on loan at Lyon and has not ruled out a move this January either.

He said: “I’m only 20 years old, so I’ll see how things develop. I just want to play, be happy and help my team-mates.

“I don’t know what will happen in January, that’s in God’s hands. I only ask for the best for my career. Whatever is meant to happen, will happen. I will keep my feet on the ground and continue to give my best. Madrid is a wonderful city, my family is there, but I will always do whatever it takes to advance in my career.”

The former Palmeiras forward was quick to stress, however, there had been no falling out with Mourinho over his lack of playing time.

“I have a lot of faith in Mourinho,” he added. “Every day he contacts me, not to talk about football, but to ask about my personal life. I will always give everything for Real Madrid because the club is above everything, but with the affection and attention that Mourinho shows me… I am even more motivated to give everything.”

Endrick behind Real Madrid superstar Mbappe

Summer signing Yan Diomande’s impact at Madrid has made life more difficult for Endrick, who is also behind the likes of Kylian Mbappe in the pecking order.

“You know full well who we’ve got there [in the number nine position] – he’s the second-best player in the world according to the latest Ballon d’Or,” Endrick said of Mbappe.

“And we know who Kylian is. Whenever I get the chance at Real – and I did just recently after the last international break – I try to perform to the best of my ability. I’ve come on in matches for five minutes, or 10 minutes… The games where I played for the longest were against Roma and AEK Athens.

“Those were moments I made the most of. I know it’s not easy.”

Real Madrid boss Mourinho eager for Endrick to get minutes with Brazil

Endrick came on for the last five minutes against Valencia at the weekend and Mourinho admitted his frustration that he couldn’t give him more due to the depth of his squad.

The Portuguese said: “It makes me angry how many great players I have that I can’t play or start every game.

“Just look at who’s going [to the Brazil national team] with Carlo [Ancelotti]: Vinícius [Júnior,] who must play; Endrick, and if Carlo plays him, I’ll be grateful.”

articles.title: Manchester United: Carrick arrives at Carrington ahead of day of crunch talks
articles.summary: Michael Carrick's tenure at Manchester United could end this week with talks continuing over his future
articles.content:
Manchester United: Carrick arrives at Carrington ahead of day of crunch talks

Michael Carrick's tenure at Manchester United could end this week with talks continuing over his future

Last Update:

Michael Carrick arrived at Manchester United’s training ground this morning with his future at the club still shrouded in doubt.

Carrick was pictured driving into the facility at around 7.15am and is expected to take a training session with the players not away on international duty.

While he is doing that, conversations are continuing in the background with United CEO Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox set to speak to the club’s minority owner Jim Ratcliffe regarding Carrick’s future in Monaco on Wednesday.

The club briefed last night that the former England midfielder was on the brink but that no firm decision had been made. That is expected to come in the next couple of days from Ratcliffe, whose INEOS group oversee football operations at Old Trafford.

Some reports suggest Carrick will be sacked on Thursday while others believe the board may look to keep him on and improve the coaching team around him.

Ratcliffe is thought to be alarmed at the club’s current standing of 18th in the Premier League table with Carrick presiding over the club’s worst start to a top-flight season since 1986. They have won just one league game all season, at home to promoted Ipswich, and suffered mixed results in the Champions League.

It is unlikely two late comebacks from United over the past week will be enough to save Carrick. His side hit back from 2-0 down to beat Roma 3-2 on Tuesday night and then two injury-time efforts salvaged a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday afternoon.

Pochettino high on United’s wish-list

If he is sacked, United have several options. Mauricio Pochettino is the current favourite after a weekend surge in the betting. The Argentine is the current boss of the United States national team and signed a new four-year deal in August that is reported to contain a £7million release clause.

Eddie Howe and Julian Nagelsmann are the other main contenders with both men out of work.

Carrick has ruled out resigning and is hoping to ride out the storm.

Asked if he was considering walking away after the Villa game, he told Sky Sports: “I’m not. I’m quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it’s got to win games.

“We haven’t won enough games, but I expect to move forward and keep working on the things that we’ve been working on and showing a lot of the good in the game today, tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches.”

articles.title: Ballon d’Or winner Kane overlooked as Messi named to FIFPro World XI for 18th time
articles.summary: Having missed out in 2024 and 2025, Lionel Messi was today included in the FIFPro World XI for his performances for Argentina at the World Cup
articles.content:
Ballon d’Or winner Kane overlooked as Messi named to FIFPro World XI for 18th time

Having missed out in 2024 and 2025, Lionel Messi was today included in the FIFPro World XI for his performances for Argentina at the World Cup

Last Update:

Lionel Messi has been included in the FIFPro World XI for a record-extending 18th time.

The former Argentina forward led his country to the World Cup final this summer only for the defending champions to lose to Spain after extra-time.

Messi has been named in the XI every year since 2007 with the exception of 2024 and 2025.

The Inter Miami man, 39, is named in a side that is somewhat top-heavy with a front four that also includes Kylian Mbappe, Erling Haaland and Lamine Yamal. There was no place for the 2026 Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane.

The midfield three is Jude Bellingham, Vitinha and Spain’s World Cup-winning captain Rodri.

Arsenal’s David Raya is in goal, behind a back three of Achraf Hakimi, Nuno Mendes and Pau Cubarsí, who was today named the 2026 winner of the Golden Boy award.

Who votes for the FIFPro World XI?

All professional footballers are given the chance to name their best three players in each position – goalkeeper, defence, midfield and attack. Every year, around 25,000 players cast their votes.

The men’s XI is based on performances from August 4, 2025 to July 19, 2026 to incorporate the 2025/26 league seasons and the World Cup.

The players with the most votes make it into the XI.

How did the voting break down?

Raya was the outstanding candidate among the goalkeepers having helped Arsenal to the Premier League crown with a series of brilliant performances. He received 51.9% of the votes for the goalkeeping position.

Hakimi (40.9%), Cubarsi (26.8%) and Mendes (25.5%) just edged out Arsenal duo Gabriel (22.4%) and William Saliba (20.9%) among the defenders.

Rodri was the midfielder that received the most votes (33.4%), ahead of Bellingham (31.3%) and Vitinha (28.2%).

Kane was not included after coming fifth among forwards with 27.6%. He trailed Erling Haaland (28.4%), Messi (29.5%), Yamal (37.4%) and Mbappe (46%).

articles.title: Gerrard calls for Liverpool to give Mac Allister a new deal
articles.summary: Alexis Mac Allister is desperate to win a new contract at Liverpool - and Steven Gerrard believes he has done enough
articles.content:
Gerrard calls for Liverpool to give Mac Allister a new deal

Alexis Mac Allister is desperate to win a new contract at Liverpool - and Steven Gerrard believes he has done enough

Last Update:

Steven Gerrard believes Alexis Mac Allister deserves a new Liverpool deal for his performances this season.

Mac Allister still has over 18 months left on his current contract at Anfield but expressed his disappointment in September that the club had not made an attempt to negotiate fresh terms over the summer, as they did with fellow midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai and Ryan Gravenberch.

The Argentina international played a key role in his country’s run to the World Cup final in July and has carried on that good form this season after an indifferent 2025/26 campaign.

Former Liverpool captain Gerrard told The Overlap Daily, brought to you by Sky Bet: “I’ve loved him this season. I think last year, like a lot of the Argentinian players, they had a bit of a distraction with the World Cup coming up. It’s the way they are. The World Cup takes over everything in their lives. And I lived that with Emiliano Martínez when I was at Aston Villa. I just think it becomes a priority. I think it becomes a bit of a distraction. It becomes the most important thing in their lives, to be ready and not injured and make sure that the national team is the priority.

“But in terms of what I’ve seen this season, I think Alexis Mac Allister deserves a new deal, and I want Liverpool to keep him, because he’s a clever footballer.”

Mac Allister is ‘fantastic in the air for a little fella’ – former Liverpool captain Gerrard

Mac Allister scored Liverpool’s opener in Sunday’s 3-1 win at Crystal Palace, nodding in Szoboszlai’s free-kick five minutes before half-time.

“He’s a competitor, he’s aggressive, he knows the game, his understanding of the game’s top,” said Gerrard.

“He’s fantastic in the air for a little fella. I think there’s only really Michael Owen I’ve seen, who’s a similar size, who’s probably better than him in the air, but he’s a threat at set pieces. He’s helpful defending set pieces, and he’s brave, and he just knows the game. He’s got a good understanding. He’s an experienced player.

“I wouldn’t want Liverpool to lose him now. I think he’s been key to the midfield, and I felt like Liverpool as a team were a little bit soft in the opening games of the season. I see a bit more fight now and a bit more spirit and a bit more of a competitive side to this Liverpool team. I think we can get better, but I’m happy with Mac Allister and his form.”

‘You have to fancy Liverpool against Manchester United’

Liverpool went into the international break in fourth place in the Premier League table, nine points behind leaders Arsenal.

They return on November 22 with a home game against a Manchester United side that sit in the relegation zone.

United salvaged a 4-4 draw against Aston Villa on Sunday thanks to two goals in injury-time, a result that might have prolonged Michael Carrick’s stay at Old Trafford, even though there was a surge of money on Mauricio Pochettino to succeed him over the weekend.

Gerrard added: “The interesting thing on Liverpool versus United is, is it going to be under Michael Carrick? Time will tell. But you’d have to fancy Liverpool on current form. I think that goes without saying. When I watch Manchester United, I don’t fancy them against anyone, because they’re so open.

“Defensively, they look all over the place. So, the big thing is, are Liverpool going to face a United team with a different manager, or is it going to be Michael Carrick’s United? Because I’m not sure Michael and Steve Holland are getting the reaction that they would want out of this team, certainly from a defensive point of view.”

articles.summary: Spain international Pau Cubarsi has been named the winner of the 2026 Golden Boy award
articles.content:
Barcelona star Cubarsi wins 2026 Golden Boy award

Spain international Pau Cubarsi has been named the winner of the 2026 Golden Boy award

Last Update:

Barcelona centre-half Pau Cubarsi has won the 2026 Golden Boy award.

The 19-year-old has enjoyed an outstanding year for club and country after helping Barca win La Liga and then playing a key role as Spain clinched the World Cup in the United States, Canada and Mexico.

The trophy is handed out to the best Under-21 player at a European club. Cubarsi is the fifth man from Barca to win it, following in the footsteps of Lionel Messi (2005), Pedri (2021), Gavi (2022) and Lamine Yamal (2024).

Yamal was not considered this year as previous winners are exempt.

Cubarsi will be awarded the trophy at a ceremony in Turin on December 14.

The 19-year-old started each of Spain’s eight games at the World Cup and thrived alongside Aymeric Laporte at the centre of La Roja’s defence. Luis de la Fuente’s side conceded just one goal throughout the tournament – in the quarter-final win over Belgium.

He was subsequently given the FIFA Young Player Award for the outstanding talent at the tournament. He was the first defender to win the gong.

Who votes for the Golden Boy award?

It is selected by an international jury comprised of 50 journalists from the main European publications. They get to select from the 25 finalists that this year included the likes of Ayyoub Bouaddi, Warren Zaire-Emery, Yan Diomande and Luka Vuskovic.

articles.title: Former Real Madrid goalkeeper suggests Vinicius is reintegrated into the squad as Mbappe’s back-up
articles.summary: Santiago Canizares does not believe Vinicius Jr should walk back into the Real Madrid team on the left wing and has suggested an alternative role
articles.content:
Former Real Madrid goalkeeper suggests Vinicius is reintegrated into the squad as Mbappe’s back-up

Santiago Canizares does not believe Vinicius Jr should walk back into the Real Madrid team on the left wing and has suggested an alternative role

Last Update:

Former Real Madrid goalkeeper Santiago Canizares has suggested Jose Mourinho solves his Vinicius Jr problem by using him as a back-up to number nine Kylian Mbappe.

Vinicius has missed Madrid’s last four league games after being sent off for pulling the hair of Villarreal’s Nathan Saliba. His ban was made up of two matches for the offence, and two more for his angry reaction to being dismissed.

His absence has coincided with Madrid finally hitting top gear and they head into the international break on the back of four straight league wins to move up to second, three points behind Barcelona.

Vinicius has played in the Champions League wins over Roma, RB Leipzig and AEK Athens – his suspension applied to domestic games only – but has struggled to make much of an impact.

And with his preferred left-wing berth now occupied by summer signing Yan Diomande, Vinicius will struggle to find a way back into the starting XI when Madrid resume their Liga campaign at home to Celta Vigo on November 21.

Canizares, who played for Madrid between 1994 and 1998 before a long, successful career at Valencia, says the Brazil international should be used in a different role to the one he has played for the bulk of his time in Spain.

He told El Partidazo de COPE: “Now let’s see how it works. Vinicius is a player who obviously won’t go unnoticed, he [Mourinho] is not going to keep him out of the way and for me the solution is that he plays as a number nine, that he plays like Mbappé [as his back-up].”

Vinicius’ return could mean Real Madrid lose ‘good vibes’ – Canizares

Canizares says it is possible for Mbappe and Vinicius to play together but that threatens to disrupt the chemistry created by the Frenchman, Diomande and Arda Guler.

“The two on the field… the team can still win games, but they will no longer have the same identity, the same balance and the same good vibes,” added Canizares.

“A coach must do everything to have his players at the highest level, try different strategies, of play, of personal management. A bad player will always be a bad player, a very good player is a player who can have negative moments and leaves the door open to return to his normal situation.”

Canizares also feels Vinicius must work harder to fit in with the team’s current structure.

He added: ”This does not have a straightforward solution. If he [Mourinho] is capable of making Vinicius run and integrate him into the team dynamic, I will take my hat off to him.”

articles.title: Lionel Messi set to return to Argentina
articles.summary: Lionel Messi has never played a club game in Argentina but that could change early in 2027
articles.content:
Lionel Messi set to return to Argentina

Lionel Messi has never played a club game in Argentina but that could change early in 2027

Last Update:

Lionel Messi could be set for a swift return to Argentina.

Messi played his final international game for his country last month, scoring his 126th goal on his 208th appearance as Argentina beat Benin 3-0 on an emotional night in Buenos Aires.

But it now seems likely he will be back in January as part of Inter Miami’s pre-season programme. Miami are being heavily tipped to take on River Plate at the Estadio Monumental in January.

Herons boss Kily Gonzalez, himself an Argentine, confirmed the news following Miami’s regular-season-ending 3-3 draw with FC Charlotte. He said: “For me, that situation is almost confirmed. It’s a very strong possibility. Obviously, it is always good to compete against Argentine teams, like River in this case. Although there is still a long way to go to get to that moment.”

Messi yet to play club game in Argentina

Messi has never played a club game in his homeland after leaving Argentina as a boy to live in Barcelona.

Assuming the fixture against River is confirmed, it will likely take place in the second half of January with Miami preparing for the truncated 2027 MLS season that runs from February to May.

Messi ended the 2026 season as the winner of the MLS Golden Boot for the second successive year. The 39-year-old scored 26 goals and added 17 assists to finish well ahead of FC Dallas striker Petar Musa (22) and Sam Surridge of Nashville (21).

The Floridian club now head into the play-offs where they will play Columbus Crew in round one. The defending champions will be wary of a Columbus side that won eight of their last nine games to secure their spot in the post-season.

articles.content:
Manchester United manager update: Pochettino the new favourite to take over at Old Trafford

Michael Carrick continues to hold on to the Manchester United job but he faces a serious challenge to his leadership from US boss Mauricio Pochettino

Last Update:

Mauricio Pochettino has surged into the running to be the new manager of Manchester United and is now the favourite to take over at Old Trafford.

Pochettino is currently in charge of the United States national team and signed a four-year contract extension in August to take the team through to the 2030 World Cup.

But that has not prevented the bookmakers from shortening his odds to get the United job should they decide to sack Michael Carrick.

United head into the international break in the Premier League relegation zone after winning just one of their opening 10 league games. The possibility of Carrick staying on is largely down to two stirring comebacks from his players over the past week.

They trailed 2-0 to Roma in the Champions League on Tuesday night but hit back to win 3-2 and two injury-time goals against Aston Villa on Sunday saw United claim a 4-4 draw.

Carrick is now 3/1 to still be in charge on January 1 – considerably shorter odds than the 9/1 price that was being offered two weeks ago.

Pochettino is as short as 6/4 after a surge of money over the weekend on the Argentine, who has managed in the Premier League before with Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea.

Eddie Howe, who is known to have support in the United boardroom, is 4/1, ahead of Julian Nagelsmann, Antonio Conte and Unai Emery.

Carrick won’t quit United

Carrick ruled out resigning after the game with Villa yesterday, telling Sky Sports: “I’m not. I’m quite clear with what direction the club needs to go in, and it’s got to win games.

“We haven’t won enough games, but I expect to move forward and keep working on the things that we’ve been working on and showing a lot of the good in the game today, tighten up on a few mistakes and win football matches.”

But former United defender Phil Neville fears the worst for United unless they improve defensively.

He said on US TV: “Mazraoui, Heaven, Yoro, and Dalot. That back four gets you relegated. That back four gets you the sack as a manager.

“We showed courage, but we only do this after we concede goals. We can’t do that, we can’t concede goals like this. We need to play like Man Utd and go forward and create chances, play with more courage.

“If we had shown that character and courage before, then we will win more games. I don’t know why we are making it hard for ourselves.”

articles.content:
Burn added to England squad after Guehi withdraws due to injury

Marc Guehi has been replaced by Dan Burn ahead of England's games with Croatia and Spain

Last Update:

Marc Guehi has withdrawn from the England squad for this week’s Nations League games with Croatia and Spain due to injury.

Guehi was taken off at half-time of Manchester City’s defeat to Nottingham Forest on Saturday evening with an undisclosed problem and won’t be risked for the two clashes in Group A3.

England host Croatia at Wembley on Thursday before taking on the world champions in Madrid on Sunday.

Burn returns to the squad for the first time since the World Cup having been left out of the group named for the extended international break across September and October.

The 34-year-old has struggled for form and fitness with Newcastle, who have won just one of their last six games in all competitions.

An FA statement this morning read: “Dan Burn has been added to the England squad following the withdrawal of Marc Guéhi through injury. “The Newcastle United defender, who has eleven caps, joined up with the rest of Thomas Tuchel’s group at Tottenham Hotspur’s training ground on Monday.“Guéhi was substituted at half-time of Manchester City’s fixture at Nottingham Forest on Saturday and will now remain with his club.”

articles.title: Barcelona and Spain star Lamine Yamal ruled out of Czechia trip due to knee problem
articles.summary: Lamine Yamal will miss the game in Prague but Spain are confident he will be ready to take on England at the weekend
articles.content:
Barcelona and Spain star Lamine Yamal ruled out of Czechia trip due to knee problem

Lamine Yamal will miss the game in Prague but Spain are confident he will be ready to take on England at the weekend

Last Update:

Lamine Yamal won’t travel with the rest of the Spain squad for the Nations League clash with Czechia but is set to play against England at the weekend.

The Barcelona star ended last night’s win at Atletico Madrid with minor discomfort in his right knee and won’t be risked for the game in Prague. He will instead stay in Catalonia for rest and treatment.

The world champions will be confident of beating Czechia which will likely mean they will need just a point against the Three Lions in Madrid on Sunday to guarantee top spot in Group A3.

Real Sociedad forward Mikel Oyarzabal is another who will remain in Spain this midweek due to a heavy cold. Oyarzabal’s partner is due to give birth which means he could also miss the England game.

Spain coach Luis de la Fuente named a squad of 27 last week and there was no initial plan to call up a replacement. However, it was later confirmed that Liverpool winger Víctor Muñoz had been added to the squad.

De la Fuente now has six attacking players to choose from for the Czechia game: Munoz, Nico Williams, Ferran Torres, Yeremy Pino, Jorge de Frutos and Roberto Fernandez.

Rayo Vallecano forward De Frutos was called up after Sociedad winger Andre Barrenetxea sustained a muscle injury during his side’s 1-0 win against Rayo at the weekend.

Williams was also forced off in Athletic Bilbao’s draw at Osasuna but later confirmed it was merely cramp.

articles.title: Real Madrid legend gets Oviedo job
articles.summary: Oviedo have turned to a Real Madrid legend to spearhead their charge for promotion
articles.content:
Real Madrid legend gets Oviedo job

Oviedo have turned to a Real Madrid legend to spearhead their charge for promotion

Last Update:

Real Madrid legend Raul has taken over at Real Oviedo following Monday’s sacking of Julian Calero.

Calero was dismissed after just 14 games in charge having been appointed in June following Oviedo’s relegation from La Liga.

His team won 2-1 at Cadiz on Saturday and sit ninth in the table but the Pachuca Group, the club’s majority shareholders, have opted to make a change and have turned to Raul to drive their promotion challenge.

For the 49-year-old, it will be a first managerial job at first-team level.

After a glittering playing career spent mostly at Madrid, for whom he made a record 741 appearances in all competitions, as well as spells with Schalke, Al Sadd and the New York Cosmos, he went into coaching with Real Madrid Castilla, the club’s reserve team.

He twice led the team to the play-offs but resigned in 2025 after missing out on the first-team job that went to Xabi Alonso.

He will replace Calero and make his debut on the bench this Saturday when Oviedo host Girona.

Oviedo ditch Calero

A club statement on Monday morning confirmed Calero’s departure. It read: “Real Oviedo has made the decision to terminate Julián Calero’s contract as coach of the first team.

“Calero, who had a contract until June 30, 2027, stops being coach from this moment. Likewise, the coaching staff that accompanies him also ends their link with the club.

“Real Oviedo wants to thank Julián Calero and his coaching staff for their dedication, professionalism and work during their time at the club, wishing them all the best of luck in their professional future.”

articles.title: Lazio lead cut to a point as Inter bounce back from derby defeat
articles.summary: An intriguing Serie A title race took another early swing.
articles.content:
Lazio lead cut to a point as Inter bounce back from derby defeat

An intriguing Serie A title race took another early swing.

Last Update:

Inter Milan bounced back from their derby defeat to AC Milan by returning to winning ways in Serie A with a 2-0 victory over Como.

Both Inter and Como tasted victory in the Champions League this week, though Inter’s win over Feyenoord was much less emphatic than the record-tying 9-1 victory Cesc Fabregas’ men enjoyed at Lens.

However, his free-scoring side were kept at bay at San Siro, where Pio Esposito put Inter ahead in the 12th minute as he turned home from Djed Spence’s low centre.

Marcus Thuram lashed home a second seven minutes later after Como failed to deal with another ball into the box, and that proved to be enough for Inter to take the points.

The win moved Inter within a point of league leaders Lazio, who were held to a 1-1 draw at Napoli.

Davide Frattesi put Lazio in front in the first half, but an own goal from Alfonso Pedraza secured a share of the spoils.

Milan built on their derby win by winning 2-1 at Genoa to move within five points of Lazio. Alphadjo Cisse and Christian Pulisic were on target in the first half before a late consolation for the hosts.

Juventus’ inconsistent season continued as they were held to a 2-2 draw by Fiorentina, Bremer’s second-half equaliser earning a point for the Bianconeri after they twice fell behind in Florence.

Elsewhere in Serie A, Atalanta won 1-0 at Monza.

Betis and Sociedad win in LaLiga, Leverkusen claim derby spoils

Barcelona re-established their three-point lead atop LaLiga by winning 2-1 at Atletico Madrid, while Real Betis and Real Sociedad each claimed valuable wins in their pursuit of Champions League football.

Betis were 2-0 victors at Elche thanks to late goals from Riquelme and Marc Bartra, and Sociedad beat Rayo Vallecano 1-0.

Villarreal left it late to see off Getafe 2-0, with the day’s other game between Celta Vigo and Levante ending 0-0.

In the Bundesliga, Aleix Garcia scored a stunning free-kick as Bayer Leverkusen won their derby with Cologne, his first-half curler and a second-half effort from Patrik Schick enough to claim an away win that moves Leverkusen up to fifth.

Third-placed Freiburg saw off Union Berlin 2-0, while Schalke are without a win in seven games after losing 2-1 at Hoffenheim.

Lille were the big winners of the day in Ligue 1, Nathan Ngoy’s decisive header giving them a 2-1 victory at Rennes that moved them second.

Lens’ nightmare week ended with a 2-1 home defeat to Marseille, Lyon were beaten 2-0 by Brest, and Monaco’s poor form continued as they conceded a 90th-minute equaliser in a 1-1 draw with Le Mans.

Nice claimed a fourth win in five, overcoming Angers 2-0 to move ahead of Monaco and Rennes and into sixth.

Le Havre are still awaiting their first win, Ligue 1’s bottom club enduring another difficult day as they lost 2-0 at home to Lorient.

articles.title: Brighton ‘not in title race’ after going second, Bournemouth make it eight in a row
articles.summary: Diego Gomez's stunner helped send the Seagulls second.
articles.content:
Brighton ‘not in title race’ after going second, Bournemouth make it eight in a row

Diego Gomez's stunner helped send the Seagulls second.

Last Update:

Pascal Gross does not believe Brighton and Hove Albion are in the Premier League title race, despite his side going second in the table with a 2-0 win over 10-man Brentford.

Brighton took the lead in the 15th minute as Diego Gomez found the top-left corner with a stunning half-volley after Brentford failed to clear a cross into the box.

Brentford were then reduced to 10 men as striker Igor Thiago was sent off following a VAR review for striking Chema Andres in the face during an off-the-ball confrontation. Thiago was originally booked, but Michael Oliver upgraded the card to a red after consulting the pitchside monitor.

Gross doubled Brighton’s lead before half-time from the penalty spot after Keane Lewis-Potter dragged down Luka Vuskovic at a corner.

There was no way back for Brentford from there as Brighton leapfrogged Manchester City into second, though Gross dismissed suggestions of the Seagulls challenging leaders Arsenal.

“We are not in a title race. But we have started the season really well. It’s the beginning of the season,” Gross told Sky Sports.

“You see the Premier League, the margins, you look at the results – we are not getting carried away yet.

“Every game we have to suffer a lot. Sometimes it is momentum. But we are really pleased to head into the international break like this.”

Bournemouth moved above Brentford and into seventh with their eighth win in a row in all competitions as they beat Ipswich Town 2-1.

Evanilson put Bournemouth in front as he pounced on a dreadful error from Ipswich goalkeeper Christian Walton.

Walton was caught in possession by Evanilson in the fifth minute, the Brazilian given the simple task of rolling into an empty net.

It was 2-0 early in the second half as Ryan Christie’s effort was deflected in by the unfortunate Leif Davis.

Jack Clarke’s penalty gave Ipswich hope, but they could not find an equaliser.

Sunderland suffer huge blow as Xhaka limps off against Chelsea

It's another worry for Regis Le Bris.

Last Update:

Sunderland suffered another setback in a hugely disappointing start to the season as Granit Xhaka limped off after just three minutes against Chelsea.

The Black Cats went into Sunday’s clash bottom of the Premier League and without a win in the league since August.

Experienced midfielder Xhaka was instrumental to Sunderland’s success last season following promotion from the Championship as Regis Le Bris’ men secured a seventh-placed finish and a place in the Europa League.

But Sunderland have struggled mightily this season as they manage both domestic and European commitments, and a spell on the sidelines for the Switzerland international would be a massive blow to their hopes of climbing the table.

Xhaka was able to walk off, but the concern over his fitness will present a significant headache for Le Bris, though he does at least have the benefit of the international break to aid his recovery from injury.

The 34-year-old was replaced by Jules Ahoka.

Sunderland visit Aston Villa in their next game after the international break.

Sunday's Tip of the Day features Liverpool and Chelsea going against Premier League strugglers.

Fabian Hurzeler’s men can go second with a win after Manchester City’s loss at Nottingham Forest on Saturday and, against an inconsistent Brentford side, we’re making a Seagulls victory the third leg of our treble.

articles.title: Jose Mourinho blasts La Liga over Real Madrid fixture schedule: ‘It’s a joke – leave us alone’
articles.summary: Jose Mourinho has slammed La Liga for Real Madrid’s congested fixture schedule.
articles.content:
Jose Mourinho blasts La Liga over Real Madrid fixture schedule: ‘It’s a joke – leave us alone’

Jose Mourinho has slammed La Liga for Real Madrid’s congested fixture schedule.

Last Update:

Jose Mourinho has launched a furious attack on La Liga’s fixture scheduling, accusing the competition’s organisers of treating Real Madrid unfairly and demanding they “leave us alone”.

The Real Madrid manager was unhappy with the limited recovery time afforded to his players following their Champions League trip to AEK Athens, questioning why his side had been given a more demanding schedule than Barcelona and Atletico Madrid.

Asked whether he had a message for Tebas and La Liga, the Portuguese coach initially insisted he needed to remain respectful before delivering a his dig.

“No, no message, I have to stay humble, because they have all the power,” Mourinho said.

“All I ask is that they don’t do things like this to us again, where we play on Sunday, then Wednesday, then Saturday, it makes no sense, it’s a joke.

“Barca and Atleti played on Tuesday and Sunday, so why should we play Wednesday and Sunday, and have to sleep at Valdebebas, because we landed from Athens at 3am?” he continued.

“I ask them to leave us alone.”

His revelation that Madrid’s players were forced to sleep at the club’s Valdebebas training complex after landing from Athens at 3am illustrates the disruption caused by their European commitments.

articles.title: Enzo Maresca admits Man City are ‘conceding too many goals’ but insists ‘no panic’ after third straight defeat
articles.summary: Enzo Maresca has opened up on another painful defeat for Manchester City.
articles.content:
Enzo Maresca admits Man City are ‘conceding too many goals’ but insists ‘no panic’ after third straight defeat

Enzo Maresca has opened up on another painful defeat for Manchester City.

Last Update:

Manchester City manager Enzo Maresca has admitted his side are conceding too many goals after suffering a third consecutive Premier League defeat, but insists there is no reason to panic.

City were punished for a poor first-half performance in the 3-1 loss to Nottingham Forest, falling two goals behind before attempting to mount a comeback after the break.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day, Maresca admitted City had failed to match their opponents physically during a disappointing first half.

“It’s quite clear – first half we didn’t match intensity or win duels or second balls,” he said.

“First thing required in these games is intensity. We tried to react at 2-0 but it’s too late. We scored one, probably could have scored more but in transition we concede one more.”

Asked why his players had struggled to compete in the opening stages, the Italian admitted he was unsure.

“I need to analyse that. Today’s game is probably the first that we lack intensity in the first 45 minutes,” he explained.

“Second half better. Never happened before – we need to understand the reason why and try not to let them happen again.”

Man City boss insists there is ‘no panic’ despite losing streak

Despite City’s recent struggles, Maresca believes his side must maintain perspective after a run of seven consecutive wins was followed by three straight defeats.

The former Chelsea boss plans to use the international break to examine what has gone wrong and address the problems affecting his team.

“[We need to] Use the international break to understand why and try to avoid in the future,” he said.

“Always concerned [about defeats] but we need balance – seven wins in a row not happened then three in a row. Need the balance.”

Maresca finished with a clear message about the mood within the City camp.

“No panic. We need to understand but no panic.”

articles.title: Mikel Arteta praises Arsenal players for ‘remarkable’ start to the season
articles.summary: Mike Arteta has spoken after Arsenal’s 1-0 win over Hull.
articles.content:
Mikel Arteta praises Arsenal players for ‘remarkable’ start to the season

Mike Arteta has spoken after Arsenal’s 1-0 win over Hull.

Last Update:

Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has hailed his players for their remarkable run of performances ahead of the international break, while admitting he was confused by a controversial penalty decision in the 1-0 win over Hull on Saturday.

Speaking to BBC Match of the Day after the final whistle, Arteta praised his squad for maintaining their standards during a demanding run of fixtures.

“Very happy with the performance and the victory as well. I think it is time to praise my players,” he said.

“What they have done not only today but after the international break is remarkable because of the games.

“We had to wait and be patient in the last part of the game to make the difference and win the game,” he explained.

“We kept generating chances, the final pass was missing or the last shot was blocked.

“We said at half-time if this is the case it will go all the way to full time but at some point it would come.”

Despite being pleased with Arsenal’s attacking play, Arteta believes there is still room for improvement when it comes to converting opportunities.

“We have some great moments, we need to put the chances we are creating against the opponent into the scoreline,” he added.

“That is what we need to improve.”

Arsenal boss questions confusing penalty decision

Arteta also addressed a controversial refereeing decision after Arsenal were denied a penalty following a VAR review.

Kai Havertz was pulled down in the penalty box, but was not awarded a penalty due to the German being in an offside position.

Arteta was left uncertain about the explanation after an offside decision prevented Arsenal from being awarded the spot-kick.

“I don’t know. When they called the referee to the monitor I thought it was a penalty but then I heard the decision was made because of the offside decision,” Arteta said.

“We don’t have clarity on it.”

articles.title: Daniel Farke claims Jayden Bogle a ‘butterfly’ after defender escapes red card in Leeds’ win over Tottenham
articles.summary: Daniel Farke says Jayden Bogle should not have been sent off against Tottenham.
articles.content:
Daniel Farke claims Jayden Bogle a ‘butterfly’ after defender escapes red card in Leeds’ win over Tottenham

Daniel Farke says Jayden Bogle should not have been sent off against Tottenham.

Last Update:

Leeds United manager Daniel Farke has defended Jayden Bogle following his challenge on Mathys Tel during Saturday’s 1-0 win over Tottenham, insisting the defender had no intention of hurting the Spurs forward.

Bogle came under scrutiny after a collision with Tel left the Tottenham player injured, but Farke was quick to dismiss suggestions that his defender had acted maliciously.

The Leeds boss described Bogle as one of the gentlest players in the Premier League, revealing that he affectionately refers to him as his “butterfly”.

Speaking to TNT Sports after the match, Farke was asked about Bogle’s involvement in the incident that left Tel injured.

“I haven’t watched it back. I have heard there were several doubtful situations. A possible hand ball,” Farke said.

“I just know that Jayden Bogle out of any bad intention. It looked like a coming together.

“It’s very unlucky outcome that Mathys is injured and we wish him all the best and he can recover quickly,” he added.

“The last thing Jayden Bogle is a nasty player. He’s possibly the softest player in the whole league.”

The Leeds manager then revealed the nickname he has given the defender, insisting it reflects his personality.

“I always call him my butterfly, and I can guarantee it was never out of bad intention.”

Leeds boss hails ‘fully deserved’ Tottenham win

Despite the controversy surrounding Bogle’s challenge, Farke was delighted with his side’s performance as Leeds secured all three points against Tottenham.

“We were pushing to win this game and were relentless,” Farke said.

“We showed great spirit, commitment and unity. It was a fully deserved win.”

Tip of the Day: Arsenal, Fulham and Manchester City feature in Premier League treble

Saturday's Tip of the Day sees a tasty Premier League treble on the cards.

Last Update:

Saturday’s Tip of the Day features three Premier League fixtures, with Arsenal backed to keep a clean sheet against Hull City and Fulham and Manchester City tipped to pick up three points.

The first leg of our treble is for both teams not to score when Arsenal host Hull City.

The Gunners will be strong favourites against the newly-promoted Tigers, with Mikel Arteta’s side boasting one of the strongest backlines in the top flight, which has also been boosted by the return of William Saliba.

The second leg is for Fulham to beat Newcastle United at Craven Cottage.

The Cottagerts will be looking to make home advantage count against the Magpies, who have been in dire form under Matthias Jaissle.

Our final selection is for Manchester City to beat Nottingham Forest at the City Ground.

articles.summary: Venezia claimed their second win through a stunning decisive goal.
articles.content:
Venezia win battle at bottom of Serie A, Gladbach’s sorry start continues in Bundesliga

Venezia claimed their second win through a stunning decisive goal.

Last Update:

Kike Perez scored a stunning winner to help Venezia move off the bottom of Serie A as they leapfrogged Udinese with a 2-1 home victory.

Udinese have been mainstays in Serie A since their promotion back to the top flight in 1995. However, they appear to be in significant danger of relegation this season.

Indeed, I Friulani are now rock bottom of the table following their latest defeat, which marked their eighth of the season.

Venezia took the lead eight minutes into the second half when Toma Basic slotted home, only for Matias Moreno’s own goal to level matters.

However, Perez sealed the points for Venezia in style, his effort from a little over 20 yards bending beautifully into the top-right corner.

In the Bundesliga, Borussia Monchengladbach remain at the foot of the table after a 3-1 defeat at Hamburg.

Miro Muheim’s long-range effort put Hamburg in front, but Gladbach were given hope of a rare positive result just before half-time when Joe Scally’s strike deflected in off team-mate Robin Hack.

Yet Ko Itakura’s second yellow card four minutes into the second half reduced Gladbach to 10 men, and Hamburg took advantage with goals from Shafiq Nandja and Albert Gronbaek.

Elsewhere, Sevilla and Alaves drew 0-0 in LaLiga, while Toulouse beat Strasbourg 3-1 in Ligue 1.

articles.title: ‘I’m at peace with my decision’ – Portugal boss feels no guilt over Ronaldo retirement
articles.summary: Jesus broke his silence on Ronaldo's abrupt end to his international career.
articles.content:
‘I’m at peace with my decision’ – Portugal boss feels no guilt over Ronaldo retirement

Jesus broke his silence on Ronaldo's abrupt end to his international career.

Last Update:

Portugal boss Jorge Jesus insisted he does not feel guilt over his part in the saga that preceded Cristiano Ronaldo‘s retirement from international football.

Ronaldo, whose 146 international goals mark an all-time record, announced his retirement from Portugal duty this week.

The Al-Nassr star made his final appearance for Portugal in September’s 1-0 Nations League win over Wales, before Jesus’ decision to leave Ronaldo as an unused substitute in their subsequent game with Norway sparked the row that essentially ended the 41-year-old’s international career.

Having gone straight down the tunnel after being left on the bench for the win over Norway, Ronaldo left the Portugal camp in Copenhagen on the eve of their clash with Denmark.

Ronaldo, who accused Jesus of breaking his word, was fined €255 (£215; $286) and given a 30-day ban by the Portuguese Football Federation.

It was expected that conciliatory talks would see Ronaldo return for Portugal’s final Nations League group games with Denmark and Wales this month.

But he instead elected to quit, though Jesus has no regrets.

Jesus, who also previously worked with Ronaldo at Al-Nassr, said: “Maybe I rushed things, but [his retirement was] not because of me. It was in his head, more call-ups, fewer call-ups.

“We also talked about it a few times. And if it was going to happen. But no, I don’t feel guilty about anything regarding his departure. I respect his decision.

“And, as such, his story cannot be ignored. He will always be a symbol and I have built a strong friendship with him over this year and a half.”

Jesus confirmed he planned to select Ronaldo for the upcoming games and had no advance warning about his retirement.

“I found out when we all did,” Jesus added. “Until then, I knew nothing about it.

“He was playing, he was scoring goals; he was one of the players on my squad list.

“All my decisions were made with the team in mind. As a manager, I have always defended what was best for the team. I am at peace with my decision.”

articles.title: Premier League Predictions: Manchester United and Chelsea frustrated but Arsenal, City and Liverpool march on
articles.summary: It's week 10 and there are some exciting games to watch out for. Here are our Premier League predictions for this weekend...
articles.content:
Premier League Predictions: Manchester United and Chelsea frustrated but Arsenal, City and Liverpool march on

It's week 10 and there are some exciting games to watch out for. Here are our Premier League predictions for this weekend...

Last Update:

We are on the eve of another Premier League weekend with some fantastic games to come.

Can Arsenal retain top spot ahead of Manchester City? Will Brighton maintain their blistering domestic form and can rock-bottom Sunderland surprise Chelsea?

Here, we list this weekend’s games and give our Premier League predictions!

FRIDAY

Everton v Coventry (8pm)Everton looked strong at Newcastle on Monday night and it may be the decision to ostracise Jack Grealish from the squad has galvanised the rest of the players. With Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall shining in midfield and Thierno Barry continuing to defy the critics and score goals, the Toffees are moving in the right direction. The same can be said for Coventry, who have won three of their last five league games to climb out of the bottom three. It is a tough ask for them tonight, though, and we fancy David Moyes to mark his record-equalling 592nd game in charge of Everton with a win.Prediction: Everton 2-0 Coventry

SATURDAY

Leeds v Tottenham (12.30pm)The mood at Tottenham has changed completely following three successive wins and they will head to Elland Road in confident mood. This is a good test of the ‘new Spurs’ under Roberto De Zerbi with the hosts strong at home. Leeds are on a poor run having taken three points from their last five games. Bizarrely, Leeds haven’t won a Premier League match that’s kicked off before 3pm since August 2022 – a run of 21 matches.Prediction: Leeds 1-1 Tottenham

Arsenal v Hull (3pm)Arsenal can go six points clear of City at the Premier League summit – for a few hours at least – with a win over Hull. The Gunners have bounced back nicely from their defeat at Brighton with four straight league wins and they seem destined to retain the title they claimed last season. Hull are in freefall having not won since August. This is a home banker.Prediction: Arsenal 3-0 Hull

Fulham v Newcastle (3pm)The pressure on Matthias Jaissle intensified following Newcastle’s limp display against Everton on MNF. The home side were booed off by the St James’ Park faithful and another defeat at Craven Cottage would mean Jaissle will be looking over his shoulder during the international break. If he needs any inspiration, he can take it from Alvaro Arbeloa. The Spaniard was in a similar situation a month ago but seven points from a possible nine has seen the Cottagers move up to 15th.Prediction: Fulham 2-0 Newcastle

Nottingham Forest v Manchester City (5.30pm)The situation is also locking bleak for Oliver Glasner. His move to the City Ground has failed to inspire Nottingham Forest and club chief Evangelos Marinakis is not known for his patience. Forest have performed better than their results suggest but there is no doubt Glasner needs to start winning games, and quickly. He is, therefore, unfortunate to come up against Manchester City this weekend. City have lost their last two Premier League games and have not lost three in a row since 2016. It is unlikely to happen here…Prediction: Nottingham Forest 1-2 Manchester City

Premier League 2026

England

SUNDAY

Brighton v Brentford (2pm)Brighton’s win at Manchester City last Saturday has prompted talk of a title challenge from Fabian Hurzeler’s men. While that may be a touch unrealistic, there is no doubt the Seagulls are set to hang around the upper end of the table for some time. Brentford’s win over Forest last weekend was much needed after a run of four games without a victory in all competitions. These two sides play good football but Brighton’s form means they go in as favourites.Prediction: Brighton 3-1 Brentford

Crystal Palace v Liverpool (2pm)Liverpool head to Selhurst Park having suffered back-to-back defeats for the first time this season – against Arsenal in the league and Fenerbahce in the Champions League. Andoni Iraola is seemingly still trying to work lout his best XI and the Merseysiders have yet to hit top gear. They will never have a better chance of achieving that than against a Palace side that look bereft. Pierre Sage has proved an underwhelming replacement for Glasner and appears a dead man walking.Prediction: Crystal Palace 0-2 Liverpool

Ipswich v Bournemouth (2pm)Thursday’s Europa League win at Sparta Prague means Bournemouth have now won their last seven games in all competitions. It is a remarkable turnaround after a slow start and they will head to Suffolk brimming with confidence. Ipswich will be pleased with their start following promotion and they sit 14th after successive draws with Forest and Hull. Portman Road is not an easy place to win but it’s impossible to go against the Cherries at the minute.Prediction: Ipswich 1-3 Bournemouth

Sunderland v Chelsea (2pm)Sunderland have been a tough watch in recent weeks. Regis Le Bris’ side have developed a nasty habit of missing chances at one end and giving away sloppy goals at the other. That is not a combination that works and the Frenchman needs to restore the physical approach that worked so well last season. Sunderland beat Chelsea in May but this is a different Blues outfit under Xabi Alonso. They still veer from the sublime to the ridiculous but they will fancy their chances of adding to Sunderland’s misery.Prediction: Sunderland 1-1 Chelsea

Manchester United v Aston Villa (4.30pm)Did United’s win over Roma offer Michael Carrick a stay of execution or will the Villa game be his final appearance in the Old Trafford dugout? Only time will tell but there is no doubt the former England midfielder needs a victory in this one to stand any chance of retaining his job. Unai Emery has no such worries and appears to be building another strong side at Villa despite a summer of churn. The visitors look a well-oiled outfit and they may be too much for United.Prediction: Manchester United 1-2 Aston Villa
